news.Content:

news.Title: Stock market today: Nasdaq and S&P 500 fall as tech stocks slide, capping volatile week
news.Content: US stocks fell on Friday, led lower by the tech ( XLK ) sector amid continued scrutiny of AI, with software and semiconductor stocks also declining. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 ( ^IXIC ) fell 1.4%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) slipped 0.6% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) wavered near the flatline. All three major averages closed in the green on Thursday. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were on track for weekly losses after a sell-off in chips earlier this week. The Dow, meanwhile, was on pace to finish the week up roughly 1%. Semiconductor stocks edged lower following a volatile week for the sector, a key driver of this year's AI trade. Shares of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave ( CRWV ) came under pressure again on Friday amid concerns over its debt-heavy balance sheet. The stock rebounded on Thursday after Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang voiced optimism about the neocloud provider. Investors have been rotating out of Tech ( XLK ) and into defensive sectors such as Health Care ( XLV ), which climbed to record highs. Tesla ( TSLA ) shares rose more than 1% after the EV maker unveiled a jaw-dropping redesign of the Roadster . Earnings season continues with Tesla on deck for next week. Streaming giant Netflix ( NFLX ) and social media giant Meta ( META ) will also post quarterly results. LIVE 11 updates 34 mins ago Ines Ferré Tesla's flying Roadster is more fuel for SpaceX merger rumors than a real car Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban reports: Tesla, strictly speaking, is a car company. But CEO Elon Musk has gone out of his way to tell investors he doesn't want it to be. The adrenaline-soaked Roadster EV unveiling — packed with aerial acrobatics — was another reminder. Tesla ( TSLA ) was showing off its newest, fastest car. But it was also, in the eyes of many analysts, soft-launching a merger with SpaceX , of engineering, audacious flair, and Musk's ambitions. Today at 3:17 PM UTC Jared Blikre Salesforce, ServiceNow reverse lower as chips try to hold lows Most S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) stocks are still rising, and chip stocks are recovering some lost ground. But software's early gains are giving way to broad selling. Roughly 70% of S&P 500 stocks are advancing, down from nearly 80% earlier. Meanwhile, the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) is bouncing after a test of its earlier lows. Nvidia ( NVDA ) turned positive briefly before heading lower again. Software is heading the other way. Salesforce ( CRM ), ServiceNow ( NOW ), and Atlassian ( TEAM ) have surrendered early gains and are each losing more than 3%. Twilio ( TWLO ) is sliding about 10%. In a Yahoo Finance basket of 45 software stocks, 41 are falling, erasing roughly $130 billion in combined market value today. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF ( IGV ) is losing nearly 3%, leaving its October gain close to zero. The recent recovery hasn't disappeared entirely. More than half the stocks in the software basket remain higher for the week. Watch whether software finds buyers as chips try to recover. Continued selling would suggest the pressure within tech is again stretching beyond the semiconductor trade. Today at 2:10 PM UTC Jared Blikre Warsh stays quiet as October hike bets fade and inflation broadens Fed chair Kevin Warsh isn't committing to another rate hike this month, and traders are increasingly betting he'll wait — despite inflation data showing price pressures reaching more of the economy. The odds of an October hike are falling to roughly 15%, according to Bloomberg's bond futures pricing, down from 33% after Wednesday's hot consumer price report and 24% before its release. That retreat began before Warsh spoke at the IMF gathering in Bangkok, where he declined to preview the Fed's next decision . "I don't prejudge meetings," he said. Treasury yields are retreating too. The 10-year yield ( ^TNX ) is hovering near 5.07%, roughly 29 basis points below its October 7 intraday high. The 30-year yield ( ^TYX ) is near 5.42%, down roughly 32 basis points from its peak that same day. Both are edging lower again today. The inflation details are less reassuring. Bank of America calculates that 55% of the core consumer price basket is experiencing three-month annualized increases above 2.5%. Its economists still expect an October hike. That connects to a concern Warsh raised at Jackson Hole in August : how widespread price increases remain. His analysis examined a different inflation measure, personal consumption expenditures, but similarly looked beyond the headline number to gauge underlying pressures. Traders aren't abandoning further tightening. Futures still price roughly one quarter-point hike by December. Watch whether inflation pressures keep broadening when the government releases its PCE inflation report on October 29 following the next Fed decision the day before. Today at 1:45 PM UTC Jared Blikre Visa, Mastercard hit records as chips sink Nearly four in five S&P 500 stocks are advancing this morning, with Visa ( V ) and Mastercard ( MA ) among the companies reaching record highs even as chip stocks extend their selloff. Advancers are outnumbering decliners by nearly 4 to 1, with nearly 400 stocks higher and about 100 lower. Ten of the 11 S&P 500 sectors are gaining, led by financials ( XLF ) and energy ( XLE ). New intraday highs are stretching well beyond the payments sector. MetLife ( MET ), McKesson ( MCK ) and Expeditors International ( EXPD ) are also setting records, alongside ConocoPhillips ( COP ) and Box ( BOX ). The Dow Jones US consumer finance ( ^DJUSSF ) and reinsurance ( ^DJUSIU ) indexes are joining them. Chips remain a different story. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) is losing more than 2%, setting up for a ninth straight decline — the first since 2006. In a Yahoo Finance semiconductor basket, 57 of 60 stocks are falling. Watch whether the broad buying holds through the session. That would strengthen the case that investors are finding alternatives to the struggling AI leaders. Today at 1:34 PM UTC David Hollerith Stocks open Friday mixed US stocks largely held steady at Friday's open as investors looked for direction after a turbulent past few days. At Friday's open, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) gained 0.4% while the the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained 0.1% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell 0.3%. For the week through Thursday, the Dow is up while the Nasdaq is down and the S&P 500 is slightly lower. Today at 1:17 PM UTC Jared Blikre CoreWeave’s bear trap offers fresh bulls hope CoreWeave ( CRWV ) may have trapped fresh bears Thursday. This morning's pullback is testing the bulls. The stock is falling about 5% before the bell after Thursday's dramatic reversal. The stock briefly broke below $60, near its late-July lows, before recovering to finish nearly 6% higher. That's a bear trap — a breakdown that reverses, catching traders betting on further losses. This morning, shares have retraced roughly half the advance from Thursday's low to the overnight high. For technicians, that puts a potential entry for fresh bulls around the midpoint of the rebound — near $65 and change. "First of all, this is more sentiment driven. This is not about fundamentals," BofA Securities senior software analyst Tal Liani told Yahoo Finance when asked what would stop CoreWeave's selling. Liani maintained a Buy rating and $140 price target despite the financing concerns, as my colleague Brian Sozzi reported . The big test remains $60. Holding above it would keep the bear trap intact. A sustained recovery would bring potential resistance around $92–$93 into view, then $120. Losing Thursday's low at $60 would undermine the bullish setup. Today at 1:10 PM UTC David Hollerith Strategy shares fall over 3% as Saylor's bitcoin giant faces index-level threat Stock in Michael Saylor's bitcoin juggernaut Strategy ( MSTR ) fell more than 3% in pre-market trading on Friday after index provider MSCI announced new eligibility rules that could lead to the removal of the bitcoin giant from its global stock indexes. MSCI said Thursday it will adopt new rules to exclude certain "non-operating companies" from its indexes, including those whose primary business resembles that of an investment fund rather than a traditional operating company. Exclusion could include Strategy, the world's largest corporate holder of bitcoin, along with other digital asset treasury companies such as MetaPlanet. Exclusion is expected to force index-tracking funds to sell shares of affected companies. MSCI said it will publish a final list of affected companies on Nov. 11, with the new rules taking effect after the market closes on Nov. 30. Strategy, led by executive chairman Saylor, has previously criticized the proposal as discriminatory against digital asset treasury companies. The company currently holds about 4% of bitcoin's total supply. Today at 12:58 PM UTC Jared Blikre Stocks broadly gaining pre-market as chip selloff continues More S&P 500 stocks are rising than falling before the bell. Chip stocks are still largely heading south. Advancers among S&P 500 constituents are outnumbering decliners by more than 2 to 1, with 224 higher, 106 lower and 173 unchanged. S&P 500 futures ( ES=F ) are edging higher while Nasdaq futures ( NQ=F ) slip. Both remain negative on the week. The stealth stock buying seen this morning extends a broader rotation. Through Thursday, 366 of the S&P's components — 73% — were higher for the week. Since October 6, nearly 70% had advanced, even as the index lost roughly 1%. Chips remain under pressure. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) is falling over 1%, putting a ninth straight loss in play. Its only previous nine-session losing streak ended in May 2006. The fund subsequently fell another 17% through its July closing low two decades ago. Meanwhile, Salesforce ( CRM ) and ServiceNow ( NOW ) are each adding more than 1% after Thursday's rallies. Buyers are lifting 33 of 45 stocks in a Yahoo Finance software basket. Software — ex-cybersecurity — has been a source of strength recently, contrasting with the semis trade. Watch whether that participation survives the opening bell. Continued buying beyond chips would show investors are sticking with alternatives to the struggling leaders. Today at 12:33 PM UTC David Hollerith Regional bank stock Truist falls after 3Q profits miss Shares of Truist Financial ( TFC ) fell more than 2% pre-market after the regional banking giant posted third quarter profits that fell short of analyst expectations. The Charlotte, North Carolina-based lender reported adjusted earnings of $1.16 per share, up 12% from a year earlier but below the $1.19 expected by analysts, according to RBC Capital Markets. Reported earnings were $0.56 per share, reflecting a $1.4 billion loss from selling bonds as part of an effort to reposition its balance sheet. Truist's stock has lagged its rivals since it was born of a so-called merger of equals between BB&T and SunTrust, which closed in December 2019. The bank has since continued to overhaul parts of its business. Truist reported net interest income of $3.66 billion in the third quarter, up slightly from a year ago. The bank also said it moved to further simplify operations in the quarter. Earlier this week, Truist sold $7.7 billion in unsecured consumer loans to private equity giant Carlyle Group. That comes after it sold $5.5 billion in near-prime auto loans to Apollo Global Management last month. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.) "We delivered a solid quarter while also taking decisive actions to better position Truist for the future," the bank's new CEO Mike Lyons said in a statement. Today at 12:30 PM UTC Ines Ferré The US economy is facing two hot wars heating up at a bad time for the White House Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley reports: Yields are above multi-decade highs , both gas and diesel prices continue to climb , and critical midterm elections are around the corner. Adding to pressure on the US economy and the current administration, the world's two largest hot wars are heating up. In the Middle East, dual fronts along the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea have seen a resurgence of conflict in recent weeks that heavily disrupted oil flows in the region. Multiple tankers and container ships in the Strait of Hormuz either caught fire or sank this week in the Iran-dominated waterway. The Washington Institute has tracked more than two dozen attacks recorded since the start of the month. Today at 11:47 AM UTC Ines Ferré Tesla stock pops after unveiling Roadster with compressed air thrusters for limited flight Yahoo Finance's Pras Subramanian reports: After a two-week delay, the Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster event went off with a massive bang — a flying one. The wedge-shaped, cyberpunk-looking Roadster EV appeared in front of an inverted half roller coaster ramp erected at SpaceX's facility in Waco, Texas. The Roadster cruised halfway up — glued to the ramp using a vacuum fan system — then launched off the ramp upside down and performed flips in the air, using air thrusters to right itself and land on the tarmac. Surging Treasury yields and macro headwinds have heavily pressured rate-sensitive stocks and market breadth, driving equal-weighted S&P 500 underperformance. While rising inflation, energy price spikes, and higher interest rates continue to pressure broader equities, the firm is actively deploying capital into compelling new positions, recently adding Toll Brothers, Hermès, and TJX Companies. Also, check the strategy's top five holdings to see its best picks in 2026.

In its Q3 2026 investor letter, Wedgewood Partners highlighted Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ: META ) as a standout performer this quarter. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META), the parent company of dominant social media platforms, is a multinational technology company that develops products to connect people. On October 15, 2026, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) closed at $736.72 per share with a $1.88 trillion market capitalization. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) posted an 11.61% YTD gain, trading within a 52-week range of $520.26 to $779.82.

Wedgewood Partners stated the following regarding Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) was another standout performer in the portfolio this quarter. Revenues grew 28%, and the Company launched a slew of AI products and updates that the market viewed positively. Meta has a long history of launching massive, objectively successful products. Yet the market often ignores them or even penalizes them. While Meta's Metaverse investments are a clear reason to be skeptical that management will bat 1.000, they are hardly a reason to discount every clear and obvious home run, or even grand slam. More recently, the Company's Threads app, launched just 3 years ago, has over 500 million monthly active users. This quarter, Meta also rolled out its Muse Agent, which users can set on autopilot to handle mundane but productive tasks like lowering phone bills or renewing license plate tags. The Muse Agent works in tandem with a private virtual machine (we estimate its value at $500 to $1,000) that every user gets for free and that maintains the user's privacy and security throughout the process.

While it is still early days, the Company's advancements on the LLM frontier, along with its long history of working with encryption, especially through WhatsApp, have made the rollout and execution of Muse Agent among the best since OpenAI launched ChatGPT. Over the next several years, we think Meta has plenty more AI products and investments that will generate returns on par with those of past years."

Wedgewood Partners stated the following regarding Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) was a top contributor to third-quarter outperformance. The Company grew operating income by about 18%, and we estimate its average gross asset base grew in the low 20s, leading to continued healthy returns on invested capital of almost 30%. These returns are virtually unchanged from a year ago and even from two years ago, when the AI buildout was in its infancy. This is strong financial evidence that Microsoft's capital allocation has delivered exceptional shareholder returns so far. For example, Microsoft has generated an incremental $35 billion in gross cash flow on $115 billion in average incremental assets over the past 12 months. The market has struggled to grasp this value creation, as the Company is rationally reinvesting that gross cash flow into higher-earning assets, causing free cash flow to dip for now. On the one hand, markets seem to love private AI labs hemorrhaging cash; on the other, markets penalize public companies when free cash flow declines, even when they can capture very high, obvious investment returns. This mispricing may be mostly technical, as the flood of "AI" stock issuance is forcing investors (including index huggers) to sell the next best thing (Microsoft) to fund expensive, less-profitable IPOs. We continue to view Microsoft as an excellent business that has executed extremely well during this AI buildout, and we expect more upside as it reaps returns on capex."

news.Title: Tesla Just Unveiled a Flying Car That Leverages SpaceX Technology. Is This the Next Big Catalyst For the Stock?
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) Founder and CEO Elon Musk has always been on the cutting edge of technology.

Musk was the first to commercialize electric vehicles, and his other company, Space Exploration Technologies Corp. , was also the first to pioneer reusable rockets.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

In recent years, Tesla has launched what it hopes will soon be a fully self-driving robotaxi fleet and is set to begin production of Optimus Humanoid robots.

But there seems to be no end to the trillionaire entrepreneur's ambitions. Recently, Musk debuted Tesla's next-generation Roadster at a demonstration in Texas, and the event did not disappoint.

The Roadster climbed a vertical ramp, went upside down, then righted itself before using cold-gas thrusters and ultra-high-pressure air tanks to hover above the ground and safely land.

Some versions of the Roadster will also reportedly be able to reach 60 miles per hour in under one second and top out at 230 mph. The electric vehicle can also travel 300 miles on a single charge.

The demonstration truly looked like something you would see in a futuristic movie. Is this the next big catalyst for Tesla stock?

Image source: Tesla.

Not likely to make a financial dent

While the Tesla Roadster is an extraordinary demonstration, it's unlikely to have a true financial impact, at least any time soon.

Tesla said production will begin in 2028. Currently, people looking to reserve these vehicles can put a deposit of $50,000 for the "Performance" version and $250,000 for the "Thrust" version.

The vehicle is more likely a way for Tesla and SpaceX to showcase their superior technological capabilities.

"Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a research note last month, according to Reuters.

Similar to other Tesla products and vehicles, this version of the Roadster has been promised for some time, with Musk initially unveiling the concept in 2017 and saying deliveries could begin in 2020.

Given the high price of the vehicle, it's not one the public can broadly afford. I would also assume there would be some pretty big regulatory hurdles to clear to allow these vehicles on the road.

Story Continues

There is another underlying catalyst

While the Roadster may not be a massive seller, many analysts and investors view the demonstration as further evidence that SpaceX will eventually merge with Tesla, a deal that has long been rumored.

Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management had two takeaways on the Roadster demonstration:

"It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Munster wrote on X. "Elon can't wait to bring $TSLA and $SPCX together."

Following the Roadster event, the odds of such a tie-up happening on Kalshi before May 1 of 2027 jumped from about 40% a few days ago to 60%, as of this writing.

The broader belief in the market is that a SpaceX-Tesla merger would make sense because both are heavily investing in technologies like AI and robotics that could complement each other's businesses. The two are also building a massive terafab facility together.

A merger could also potentially help Musk gain greater control of Tesla, where Musk owns about 20% of outstanding shares. Meanwhile, Musk owns over 48% of outstanding SpaceX shares, but roughly 82% of total voting power.

If Tesla is acquired, it might be done so at a premium, which would lift the stock.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

Bram Berkowitz has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Tesla. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy .

news.Title: Tesla's flying Roadster is more fuel for SpaceX merger rumors than a real car
news.Content:
Tesla, strictly speaking, is a car company. But CEO Elon Musk has gone out of his way to tell investors he doesn't want it to be. The adrenaline-soaked Roadster EV unveiling — packed with aerial acrobatics — was another reminder.

Tesla ( TSLA ) was showing off its newest, fastest car. But it was also, in the eyes of many analysts, soft-launching a merger with SpaceX , of engineering, audacious flair, and Musk's ambitions.

The reactions from Tesla's sharpest observers underscored what was left unsaid. "So SpaceX buys Tesla this year. That's has become obvious," wrote Gerber Kawasaki's Ross Gerber, a vocal Tesla shareholder and frequent commentator on Musk's business moves.

In, of course, a post on X.

The flashy Roadster unveiling placed an exclamation point on simmering chatter about an impending tie-up . Rumors and commentary have been circulating for months, highlighting the shared technology and partnerships that would make for a sensible marriage. Musk himself has heavily hinted at combining his two biggest companies, including on Tesla's latest earnings call. And last month, at the All-In Summit, he emphasized the collaboration between the two.

In a note to clients earlier this month, Barclays analyst Dan Levy said a tie-up "has increasingly become the consensus expectation." The Roadster event — light on details about the actual car business, but heavy on the pizzazz — prompted several other Tesla watchers to hint at or explicitly get behind that forecast.

A note by JPMorgan analysts led by Rajat Gupta pointed to Tesla glossing over what the Roadster means commercially for Tesla, instead showcasing its deep collaboration with SpaceX. Other reactions were more direct.

Gene Munster of Deepwater Management posted his two big takeaways on X , Thursday night. "1. It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers. 2. Elon can't wait to bring Tesla and SpaceX together."

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives said the event strengthened the case for Musk's rocket company and Tesla to operate as one engineering platform. "We believe there is an 80% chance that Tesla and SpaceX merge by the end of 2027 for a number of strategic AI/data driven reasons," he said in a note on Friday.

Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban .

news.Title: 'There's no point': Tesla Roadster's splashy reveal doesn't mean a merger with SpaceX
news.Content:
The Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster reveal reignited chatter that Elon Musk should finally merge Tesla and SpaceX ( SPCX ), a move he has long been rumored to want to make.

But maybe he doesn't need to do it right away, if at all.

"If I was on the board of Tesla or SpaceX, I would challenge Elon on the point of why not just mash them together?" tech analyst EMJ Capital founder Eric Jackson said on Sozzi Unleashed . "He certainly likes mashing his companies together, but when they're both getting a premium valuation, there's no point in mashing them together. There was a point when SolarCity was dying on the vine [so it made sense] to mash it into Tesla. There was a point when X was kind of like sitting out there [so it made sense] to mash it into SpaceX, but right now they're both getting the Elon premium."

Tesla unveiled its redesigned Roadster on Thursday night at SpaceX's ( SPCX ) rocket test site in McGregor, Texas. It came nearly nine years after Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk first showed his idea for the car in 2017.

The wait was worth it.

Using cold-gas thrusters borrowed from SpaceX and a suction system, the car drove upside down on a curved ramp, vaulted off it, and flipped in midair before landing. The car also jumped over a series of Tesla vehicles — not unlike the classic move of K.I.T.T. from the "Knight Rider" TV series.

Musk said it can reach 60 mph in under a second and top 230 mph, though it is unclear whether any of the stunt features would be legal on public roads.

Tesla said production will start in 2028. There is a $50,000 deposit on the Performance version and $250,000 on the Thrust version.

Tesla stock rose as high as 2% while SpaceX advanced 1% in early trading on Friday before paring gains.

"We believe this is a small example of the synergies between Tesla and SpaceX and we believe there is an 80% chance that Tesla and SpaceX merge by the end of 2027 for a number of strategic AI/data driven reasons," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said.

news.Title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its third quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 15, 2026, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) projected full-year 2026 revenue growth of around 44% in U.S. dollar terms. Sustained global demand for leading-edge semiconductors gives the chipmaker pricing power and revenue visibility through multiyear capital cycles. Expanding physical manufacturing capacity ensures the company captures expanding artificial intelligence workloads while shielding market share from foundry rivals. Three takeaways from the call highlight its strategic trajectory.

1. Production Capacity for Next-Generation 2-Nanometer Chips Will Double by 2027

The 2-nanometer (N2) chip production node represents the leading edge of semiconductor manufacturing, providing higher processing speed and lower energy consumption. Doubling N2 output secures technical leadership as global customers demand advanced silicon for artificial intelligence (AI) software and smartphone applications.

N2 is ramping successfully in multiple phases at both Hsinchu and Kaohsiung site. We expect our N2 family technologies annual capacity to more than double in 2027, supported by strong demand from both smartphone and HPC AI applications.

-- C.C. Wei, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer

2. Unprecedented Factory Expansion Keeps Competitors From Stealing Market Share

Management maintains high spending on capital expenditures (CapEx), or investments in manufacturing facilities and machinery, to construct nearly 20 chip fabrication plants (fabs) globally. Rapid facility expansion allows the company to absorb rising market demand while preventing competing foundries from capturing market share.

We are moving full speed ahead to increase our capacity to meet our assessed demand, and stepping up our CapEx investment to support our customers' future growth. TSMC is expanding at unprecedented pace with a nearly 20 fabs worldwide in progress.

3. The Transition to Agentic Artificial Intelligence Is Accelerating Chip Demand

Artificial intelligence software is transitioning from basic conversational chatbots to autonomous agentic systems that execute complex multi-step workflows. This structural shift increases processing workloads, which requires larger quantities of high-performance computing (HPC) chips.

The AI market continues to be very strong. Recent developments are very positive to AI's long-term demand outlook. We observe increasing AI demand fueled by the rising adoption of agentic AI as we transition from chatbot to AI assistance.

Story Continues

Looking Ahead

Chip demand across artificial intelligence and mobile platforms stretches capacity, and management isn't hiding its satisfaction. Scale advantages and customer integration strengthen its competitive moat.

With our technology leadership, manufacturing excellence, global capacity expansion, and customer trust, we are well-positioned to capture the full multi-year structural AI-related demand.

Expanding overseas plants requires careful cost control to protect long-term margins.

Overall, with our fundamental competitive advantages of manufacturing technology leadership and large-scale production base, we are confident that TSMC continues to be the most cost-efficient manufacturer in every region that we operate.

-- Wendell Huang, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

news.Title: 2 Tech Stocks to Buy Now and Hold for a Decade (Hint: 1 Isn't in the AI Trade)
news.Content:
Investors understandably tie today's technology industry to artificial intelligence (AI). Since cutting-edge technology has driven much of the innovation, investors could easily fall into the trap of assuming that all tech companies are AI enterprises as well.

Nonetheless, in many tech enterprises, AI is more of a secondary growth driver. Given that, tech stocks like Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Sea Limited (NYSE: SE) should continue to drive long-term growth, even though only one is an AI company.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The AI company: Amazon

Most of the public knows Amazon best for its e-commerce platform. This is crucial because no matter where one stands on the state of the market, the e-commerce part of the business is highly recession-resistant due to the wide variety of goods it offers.

However, even with faster-growth businesses like digital advertising and third-party seller services, its retail business is generally a slower-growth, lower-margin segment.

Instead, most of its growth comes from its AI-driven cloud arm, Amazon Web Services (AWS). Despite accounting for just 21% of the company's revenue in the first half of 2026, it delivers the majority of the company's operating income.

With that, Amazon reported $382 billion in net sales in the first two quarters of 2026, an 18% increase from the same period in 2025.

Admittedly, its net income points to struggles. Even though it reported $92 billion in profit in the first half of 2026, $69 billion came from investment gains. Thus, when subtracting those increases, Amazon's net income barely grew over the same period.

Other income also skewed its P/E ratio down to 21, an unusually low level for Amazon. Furthermore, after decades of reporting massive free cash flows, it reported a $7.6 billion outflow over the trailing 12 months. With the company pledging $220 billion in capital expenditures (capex), the cost of keeping up in the AI race has strained its balance sheet.

Nonetheless, its 31 forward P/E ratio suggests its valuation is well below historical levels. Additionally, the spending that has strained the balance sheet and income statement is an investment that should make the upside worth the risk . Thus, it likely pays to be patient with Amazon stock.

The non-AI company: Sea Limited

Story Continues

In one respect, Sea Limited is the non-AI version of Amazon, with a leading e-commerce business, Shopee.

It differs from Amazon in that it operates a fintech enterprise, Monee, which continues to gain traction in its home region of Southeast Asia. Also, the company started as a gaming company, Garena, which survives today and is best known for the popular mobile game Free Fire . All three businesses are recession-resistant, which could mitigate stock selling in tougher times.

Fortunately, that does not appear to be a problem at the moment. In the first half of 2026, revenue increased 47% year over year to $14.9 billion, with all three segments growing in the double digits.

Its net income of $896 million grew by a more modest 9% annually, as the company increased operating expenses to invest in its business. Although the lower profit may disappoint investors now, those investments could drive revenue and profit growth later.

Moreover, since it is not an AI company, it only spent about $793 million in capex over the trailing 12 months, and the $4.9 billion in free cash flow over the same period suggests it can afford such investments.

Indeed, the investments probably led to significant declines in the stock over the last year. Still, even with slower profit growth, the stock trades at just 37 times earnings. Additionally, with a forward P/E ratio of 25 and its efforts to invest for the future, Sea Limited is arguably a stock investors should consider buying.

news.Title: 'Something extraordinary': Tesla Roadster wows with compressed air thrusters for limited flight
news.Content:
After a two-week delay, the Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster event went off with a massive bang — a flying one.

The wedge-shaped, cyberpunk-looking Roadster EV appeared in front of an inverted half roller coaster ramp erected at SpaceX's facility in Waco, Texas. The Roadster cruised halfway up — glued to the ramp using a vacuum fan system — then launched off the ramp upside down and performed flips in the air, using air thrusters to right itself and land on the tarmac.

Then the Roadster performed a similar stunt, jumping over several Teslas (including a semi), inverted itself, and then used its thrusters to land — an automaker first.

"Well, it worked," CEO Elon Musk deadpanned.

The Roadster also went 0-60 mph in less than 1 second (0.81 seconds) during a test Tesla conducted at the event. While Tesla claimed the car could hit a top speed of 230 mph, Musk boasted that the production version could target half the speed of sound, or Mach 0.5 (383 mph).

So when can you expect to get one? "We enter production in 2028," Musk said.

Tesla said the car comes in three configurations:

Performance: road-ready, seats 2, with multi-mode suction system for next-level performance on and off track;

Thrust: race-ready, seats 2, with multi-mode suction system and rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters that enable 0–60 in <1 second

Rocket: air-ready, seats 1, with multi-mode suction system, plus perimeter-mounted cold-gas thrusters for forward, upward acceleration and lateral rotational movement. So ... yes, it can fly.

Tesla said the three versions had a range exceeding 300 miles, with a top speed of up to 230 mph for the Rocket version.

Officially, in terms of performance, 0- 60 mph across the range is <1.6 seconds for Performance, <0.9 seconds for Thrust, and <0.59 seconds for Rocket.

No word yet on how the Rocket version, with its thrusters that allow short flights, would be allowed on public roads.

The event came two weeks after the initial Oct. 1 reveal date. Tesla said the reveal was pushed back due to weather conditions at the demo site, SpaceX's ( SPCX ) Rocket Development and Testing facility in Waco, Texas .

Tesla is asking prospective buyers to put down a $5,000 deposit, followed by a $45,000 wire transfer due within 10 days of the initial deposit for the performance version, and a $250,000 deposit for the thrust variant. The rocket version is invite-only; no MSRP amounts were released.

" There were hints that the Tesla Roadster might do something extraordinary, but I think what happened in Texas on Thursday evening far exceeded everyone's expectations," said Henry Catchpole, host of Hagerty's "The Driver's Seat," who was in attendance at the event. "How it all translates into a finished, usable, enjoyable road car for enthusiasts remains to be seen. For now, it seems like an incredible engineering achievement ."

Story Continues

Tesla bull Gene Munster of Deepwater Management had two big takeaways from tonight's Roadster event.

"1. It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers. 2. Elon can't wait to bring Tesla and SpaceX together," he posted on X.com .

The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever EV and used a Lotus Elise chassis.

Tesla announced its successor way back in 2017, took in reservations with those high deposits, and originally said deliveries would begin in 2020. Those initial reservation holders have been waiting for quite a long time.

During his appearance on the All-In Summit in September , Musk brought up the Tesla Roadster. "It'll be a banger. Excitement guaranteed. Success is not guaranteed, but excitement is," he added.

For Tesla fans and watchers online, the event certainly delivered — even if some of the gravity-defying features have "no commercial value."

Pras Subramanian is Lead Auto Reporter for Yahoo Finance. You can follow him on X and on Instagram .

news.Title: Stock market today: Nasdaq and S&P 500 slip as Dow rises, capping volatile week
news.Content: US stocks fell Friday as investors tried to look past AI trade-financing worries, turning their focus to upcoming earnings next week. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 ( ^IXIC ) fell 1.1% while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) slipped 0.3% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) gained 0.2%. All three major averages closed in the green on Thursday. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were on track for weekly losses after a sell-off in chips earlier this week. The Dow, meanwhile, was on pace to finish the week up roughly 1%. Semiconductor stocks edged lower following a volatile week for the sector, a key driver of this year's AI trade. Shares of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave ( CRWV ) came under pressure again on Friday amid concerns over its debt-heavy balance sheet. The stock rebounded on Thursday after Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang voiced optimism about the neocloud provider. Investors have been rotating out of Tech ( XLK ) and into defensive sectors such as Health Care ( XLV ), which climbed to record highs. Tesla ( TSLA ) shares rose more than 1% after the EV maker unveiled a jaw-dropping redesign of the Roadster . Earnings season continues with Tesla on deck for next week. Streaming giant Netflix ( NFLX ) and social media giant Meta ( META ) will also post quarterly results. LIVE 10 updates 54 mins ago Jared Blikre Salesforce, ServiceNow reverse lower as chips try to hold lows Most S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) stocks are still rising, and chip stocks are recovering some lost ground. But software's early gains are giving way to broad selling. Roughly 70% of S&P 500 stocks are advancing, down from nearly 80% earlier. Meanwhile, the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) is bouncing after a test of its earlier lows. Nvidia ( NVDA ) turned positive briefly before heading lower again. Software is heading the other way. Salesforce ( CRM ), ServiceNow ( NOW ), and Atlassian ( TEAM ) have surrendered early gains and are each losing more than 3%. Twilio ( TWLO ) is sliding about 10%. In a Yahoo Finance basket of 45 software stocks, 41 are falling, erasing roughly $130 billion in combined market value today. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF ( IGV ) is losing nearly 3%, leaving its October gain close to zero. The recent recovery hasn't disappeared entirely. More than half the stocks in the software basket remain higher for the week. Watch whether software finds buyers as chips try to recover. Continued selling would suggest the pressure within tech is again stretching beyond the semiconductor trade. Today at 2:10 PM UTC Jared Blikre Warsh stays quiet as October hike bets fade and inflation broadens Fed chair Kevin Warsh isn't committing to another rate hike this month, and traders are increasingly betting he'll wait — despite inflation data showing price pressures reaching more of the economy. The odds of an October hike are falling to roughly 15%, according to Bloomberg's bond futures pricing, down from 33% after Wednesday's hot consumer price report and 24% before its release. That retreat began before Warsh spoke at the IMF gathering in Bangkok, where he declined to preview the Fed's next decision . "I don't prejudge meetings," he said. Treasury yields are retreating too. The 10-year yield ( ^TNX ) is hovering near 5.07%, roughly 29 basis points below its October 7 intraday high. The 30-year yield ( ^TYX ) is near 5.42%, down roughly 32 basis points from its peak that same day. Both are edging lower again today. The inflation details are less reassuring. Bank of America calculates that 55% of the core consumer price basket is experiencing three-month annualized increases above 2.5%. Its economists still expect an October hike. That connects to a concern Warsh raised at Jackson Hole in August : how widespread price increases remain. His analysis examined a different inflation measure, personal consumption expenditures, but similarly looked beyond the headline number to gauge underlying pressures. Traders aren't abandoning further tightening. Futures still price roughly one quarter-point hike by December. Watch whether inflation pressures keep broadening when the government releases its PCE inflation report on October 29 following the next Fed decision the day before. Today at 1:45 PM UTC Jared Blikre Visa, Mastercard hit records as chips sink Nearly four in five S&P 500 stocks are advancing this morning, with Visa ( V ) and Mastercard ( MA ) among the companies reaching record highs even as chip stocks extend their selloff. Advancers are outnumbering decliners by nearly 4 to 1, with nearly 400 stocks higher and about 100 lower. Ten of the 11 S&P 500 sectors are gaining, led by financials ( XLF ) and energy ( XLE ). New intraday highs are stretching well beyond the payments sector. MetLife ( MET ), McKesson ( MCK ) and Expeditors International ( EXPD ) are also setting records, alongside ConocoPhillips ( COP ) and Box ( BOX ). The Dow Jones US consumer finance ( ^DJUSSF ) and reinsurance ( ^DJUSIU ) indexes are joining them. Chips remain a different story. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) is losing more than 2%, setting up for a ninth straight decline — the first since 2006. In a Yahoo Finance semiconductor basket, 57 of 60 stocks are falling. Watch whether the broad buying holds through the session. That would strengthen the case that investors are finding alternatives to the struggling AI leaders. Today at 1:34 PM UTC David Hollerith Stocks open Friday mixed US stocks largely held steady at Friday's open as investors looked for direction after a turbulent past few days. At Friday's open, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) gained 0.4% while the the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained 0.1% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell 0.3%. For the week through Thursday, the Dow is up while the Nasdaq is down and the S&P 500 is slightly lower. Today at 1:17 PM UTC Jared Blikre CoreWeave’s bear trap offers fresh bulls hope CoreWeave ( CRWV ) may have trapped fresh bears Thursday. This morning's pullback is testing the bulls. The stock is falling about 5% before the bell after Thursday's dramatic reversal. The stock briefly broke below $60, near its late-July lows, before recovering to finish nearly 6% higher. That's a bear trap — a breakdown that reverses, catching traders betting on further losses. This morning, shares have retraced roughly half the advance from Thursday's low to the overnight high. For technicians, that puts a potential entry for fresh bulls around the midpoint of the rebound — near $65 and change. "First of all, this is more sentiment driven. This is not about fundamentals," BofA Securities senior software analyst Tal Liani told Yahoo Finance when asked what would stop CoreWeave's selling. Liani maintained a Buy rating and $140 price target despite the financing concerns, as my colleague Brian Sozzi reported . The big test remains $60. Holding above it would keep the bear trap intact. Today at 1:10 PM UTC David Hollerith Strategy shares fall over 3% as Saylor's bitcoin giant faces index-level threat Stock in Michael Saylor's bitcoin juggernaut Strategy ( MSTR ) fell more than 3% in pre-market trading on Friday after index provider MSCI announced new eligibility rules that could lead to the removal of the bitcoin giant from its global stock indexes. MSCI said Thursday it will adopt new rules to exclude certain "non-operating companies" from its indexes, including those whose primary business resembles that of an investment fund rather than a traditional operating company. Exclusion could include Strategy, the world's largest corporate holder of bitcoin, along with other digital asset treasury companies such as MetaPlanet. Exclusion is expected to force index-tracking funds to sell shares of affected companies. MSCI said it will publish a final list of affected companies on Nov. 11, with the new rules taking effect after the market closes on Nov. 30. Strategy, led by executive chairman Saylor, has previously criticized the proposal as discriminatory against digital asset treasury companies. The company currently holds about 4% of bitcoin's total supply. Today at 12:58 PM UTC Jared Blikre Stocks broadly gaining pre-market as chip selloff continues More S&P 500 stocks are rising than falling before the bell. Chip stocks are still largely heading south. Advancers among S&P 500 constituents are outnumbering decliners by more than 2 to 1, with 224 higher, 106 lower and 173 unchanged. Buyers are lifting 33 of 45 stocks in a Yahoo Finance software basket. Software — ex-cybersecurity — has been a source of strength recently, contrasting with the semis trade. Today at 12:33 PM UTC David Hollerith Regional bank stock Truist falls after 3Q profits miss Shares of Truist Financial ( TFC ) fell more than 2% pre-market after the regional banking giant posted third quarter profits that fell short of analyst expectations. The Charlotte, North Carolina-based lender reported adjusted earnings of $1.16 per share, up 12% from a year earlier but below the $1.19 expected by analysts, according to RBC Capital Markets. Reported earnings were $0.56 per share, reflecting a $1.4 billion loss from selling bonds as part of an effort to reposition its balance sheet. Truist's stock has lagged its rivals since it was born of a so-called merger of equals between BB&T and SunTrust, which closed in December 2019. The bank has since continued to overhaul parts of its business. Truist reported net interest income of $3.66 billion in the third quarter, up slightly from a year ago. The bank also said it moved to further simplify operations in the quarter. Earlier this week, Truist sold $7.7 billion in unsecured consumer loans to private equity giant Carlyle Group. That comes after it sold $5.5 billion in near-prime auto loans to Apollo Global Management last month. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.) "We delivered a solid quarter while also taking decisive actions to better position Truist for the future," the bank's new CEO Mike Lyons said in a statement. Today at 12:30 PM UTC Ines Ferré The US economy is facing two hot wars heating up at a bad time for the White House Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley reports: Yields are above multi-decade highs , both gas and diesel prices continue to climb , and critical midterm elections are around the corner. Multiple tankers and container ships in the Strait of Hormuz either caught fire or sank this week in the Iran-dominated waterway. The Washington Institute has tracked more than two dozen attacks recorded since the start of the month. The wedge-shaped, cyberpunk-looking Roadster EV appeared in front of an inverted half roller coaster ramp erected at SpaceX's facility in Waco, Texas. The Roadster cruised halfway up — glued to the ramp using a vacuum fan system — then launched off the ramp upside down and performed flips in the air, using air thrusters to right itself and land on the tarmac. news.Title: Google Parent Alphabet Has a Big Surprise for Waymo
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Alphabet's ( NASDAQ:GOOG ) Waymo is taking its autonomous ride-hailing business into Canada, signing a binding framework to launch fully autonomous service in Toronto in 2028 .

The move marks another important geographic expansion for Waymo as Alphabet looks to turn years of autonomous-driving investment into a broader commercial transportation network.

Is GOOG fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Waymo plans to begin manual mapping and validation drives around Toronto in the near term, laying the groundwork for the eventual driverless rollout.

The company will work with Toronto-based Element Fleet Management to handle end-to-end fleet services.

Waymo also expects the expansion to create hundreds of jobs over time across fleet maintenance, validation driving, customer service and operations.

Expanding into Canada marks an important milestone in Waymo's global journey, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana said, adding that Waymo wants to contribute to safer streets and more accessible transportation in Toronto.

The move builds on Waymo's existing Canadian relationships.

The Canada Pension Plan Investment Board has been a long-term investor in the autonomous-driving company, while Canadian auto supplier Magna International ( NYSE:MGA ) is already a manufacturing partner.

The planned Toronto launch also shows how Waymo is beginning to move beyond proving that autonomous vehicles work toward proving that the business can be replicated across different cities, regulations and operating environments.

Investor Takeaway

I think the important part of the Toronto announcement is not simply that Waymo is entering another city.

It is that Alphabet is beginning to test whether Waymo can become a repeatable international platform .

Toronto brings different weather, regulation and operating conditions than many of Waymo's existing markets, making the expansion a potentially important test of how easily its autonomous-driving technology can scale.

The 2028 target also gives Waymo considerable time for mapping, regulatory work and fleet preparation before carrying paying passengers without drivers.

For Alphabet investors, the key things to watch are fleet size, regulatory approvals, ride volumes, geographic expansion and whether Waymo can lower the cost of operating each vehicle as scale increases .

If Toronto succeeds, Canada could become another launchpad for broader international expansion rather than a one-city experiment.

news.Title: Why SandiskStock Dropped (Again) on Friday
news.Content:
Well, it's Friday, I've got good news and bad news for investors in Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock.

Bad news first: One of the biggest names in computer memory chipmakers , Sandisk stock declined every single day so far this week, and is down again on Friday, slipping another 3.2% lower through 10:45 a.m. ET.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But now here's the good news: There's basically no new bad news.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

New news and old news

Granted, the old bad news is still in effect. On Monday, Chinese DRAM specialist CXMT, the fourth-largest computer memory maker by market share , announced it has made progress with its new "4F square" technology to increase DRAM storage density. The company plans to have a product ready for market before the end of this year, incorporating the new technology.

And it's investor fears of this new competition from CXMT that have been driving Sandisk stock lower all week long, for a total loss of 15%.

Further worries did surface this morning, of course, when the U.S. Department of Labor reported its September Consumer Price Index data. This showed inflation rising 3.7% year-over-year, 10 basis points faster than expected. Higher inflation can prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, and this is generally viewed as bad news for tech companies because it raises the cost of debt -- and debt is what a lot of companies have been using lately to buy Sandisk memory chips.

Sandisk looks safe

Still, that's a macroeconomic risk that affects all stocks. As far as SanDisk-specific concerns go, I think CXMT is still the big one weighing on investors today -- and, as I've repeatedly stated, it's an unnecessary worry.

CXMT makes DRAM. Sandisk doesn't. CXMT is therefore not a huge threat to Sandisk, and so worries about Sandisk stock seem overblown.

news.Title: Elon Musk's Roadster Dream Takes a Surprising New Turn
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) shares jumped after the company finally unveiled its redesigned Roadster, showing off a new version of the long-delayed sports car equipped with SpaceX-developed thrusters capable of lifting and rotating the vehicle in the air .

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Tesla stock rose about 4.5% in premarket trading Friday following the event.

The demonstration took place at SpaceX's McGregor, Texas, facility and featured a dramatically reworked Roadster using cold-gas thrusters derived from SpaceX technology.

Tesla showcased the vehicle performing aerial maneuvers, including jumps and mid-air rotation. The company said the most extreme version can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in under 0.6 seconds and reach speeds above 230 mph .

The Roadster now comes in several configurations.

The Performance version is designed for road use, while higher-end Thrust and Rocket variants add increasingly aggressive thruster systems. The Rocket version is invite-only and is not approved for public-road use.

The bigger question, however, remains production.

Tesla first unveiled the next-generation Roadster in 2017 and initially targeted production for 2020. After years of delays, CEO Elon Musk now says production is targeted for 2028 .

Investor Takeaway

I think the Roadster matters less because Tesla is suddenly going to sell huge numbers of $200,000-plus sports cars.

Its value is mostly symbolic.

The car functions as a halo product designed to reinforce Tesla's image as an engineering company pushing the limits of EV performance, while also showcasing deeper cooperation with SpaceX. Reuters noted that analysts see the Roadster primarily in that role rather than as a major earnings driver.

The SpaceX connection is especially notable given growing speculation about closer integration between Musk's companies.

But investors also have to weigh the spectacle against the execution record.

The Roadster is already years behind its original schedule, and production is still roughly two years away.

For Tesla shareholders, the real milestones are now whether the 2028 production target holds, what the final pricing looks like, how many vehicles Tesla can realistically produce, and whether the technologies demonstrated in the Roadster eventually migrate into higher-volume models .

The flying demonstration got attention. Delivering the car at scale is the harder test.

news.Title: Why Microchip Tech (MCHP) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again
news.Content:
Looking for a stock that has been consistently beating earnings estimates and might be well positioned to keep the streak alive in its next quarterly report? Microchip Technology (MCHP), which belongs to the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry, could be a great candidate to consider.

This chipmaker has an established record of topping earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The company boasts an average surprise for the past two quarters of 11.29%.

For the most recent quarter, Microchip Tech was expected to post earnings of $0.7 per share, but it reported $0.76 per share instead, representing a surprise of 8.57%. For the previous quarter, the consensus estimate was $0.5 per share, while it actually produced $0.57 per share, a surprise of 14.00%.

Price and EPS Surprise

For Microchip Tech, estimates have been trending higher, thanks in part to this earnings surprise history. And when you look at the stock's positive Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction), it's a great indicator of a future earnings beat, especially when combined with its solid Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Microchip Tech currently has an Earnings ESP of +3.31%, which suggests that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This positive Earnings ESP when combined with the stock's Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) indicates that another beat is possibly around the corner.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

news.Title: Will Intel (INTC) Beat Estimates Again in Its Next Earnings Report?
news.Content:
Looking for a stock that has been consistently beating earnings estimates and might be well positioned to keep the streak alive in its next quarterly report? Intel (INTC), which belongs to the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry, could be a great candidate to consider.

When looking at the last two reports, this world's largest chipmaker has recorded a strong streak of surpassing earnings estimates. The company has topped estimates by 1,450.00%, on average, in the last two quarters.

For the most recent quarter, Intel was expected to post earnings of $0.21 per share, but it reported $0.42 per share instead, representing a surprise of 100.00%. For the previous quarter, the consensus estimate was $0.01 per share, while it actually produced $0.29 per share, a surprise of 2,800.00%.

Price and EPS Surprise

For Intel, estimates have been trending higher, thanks in part to this earnings surprise history. And when you look at the stock's positive Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction), it's a great indicator of a future earnings beat, especially when combined with its solid Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Intel currently has an Earnings ESP of +1.11%, which suggests that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This positive Earnings ESP when combined with the stock's Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) indicates that another beat is possibly around the corner. We expect the company's next earnings report to be released on October 29, 2026.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

news.Title: AWS and Microsoft Face Fresh UK Scrutiny Over Cloud Switching Barriers
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN , Financials ), the owner of Amazon Web Services , is under further regulatory scrutiny in the U.K. with Microsoft over how easy it is for consumers to switch between cloud providers.Britain's Competition and Markets Authority stated on Friday that both businesses might do more to decrease obstacles to switching providers and utilizing different cloud services.It may sound complex, but it gets right down to one of the greatest features of the cloud business model: client stickiness.Large corporations typically design apps on particular cloud platforms. The harder or more costly it is to migrate your workloads elsewhere, the more price power the provider may have.The agency wants to give consumers more leeway to switch between providers or to split workloads across multiple clouds.That sets up a possible tradeoff for AWS and Microsoft.This might lead to a more competitive market, since customers are less tied to one environment and can move more easily.While the CMA has not started a full strategic market status inquiry, it noted the possibility remained under evaluation.Next to monitor is if the regulator proceeds from pressure to official action, which might compel adjustments to cloud pricing, contracts or interoperability.

news.Title: 科技股回檔是年底前上車機會？Jefferies明星分析師看好美股11、12月強攻
news.Content:
那斯達克100指數周四盤中大幅反轉，幅度創4月以來最大，被形容為「可能是10月修正開始以來最令人振奮的發展」。Jefferies分析師認為，當前震盪可能是布局年底行情前，最後幾次具吸引力的進場機會之一，並預期11月與12月將有強勁表現。

Jefferies備受推崇的技術分析師Dan Kirsch，其每日技術分析報告廣受市場關注。他在周五的報告中坦言，雖然早已預期本月波動會加劇，但科技股的疲弱程度仍超出預期。

不過，最讓Kirsch感到鼓舞的是，他先前所預期的「輪動廣度擴大」正在發生，且發酵力道比想像中更為猛烈。

Kirsch認為，近期最關鍵的發展在於科技股與其他大盤類股（以等權重S&P 500指數 RSP 為代表）之間的走勢分歧。他指出，那斯達克指數( NDX ) 雖自高點拉回約5%，但等權重S&P 500指數已自低點反彈約7%至8%。

雖然他更希望這種輪動廣度的擴展能伴隨科技股的強勢，但這對整體市場而言仍是極具建設性的積極訊號。

另一方面，BTIG技術分析師Jonathan Krinsky認為，半導體股連跌七個交易日後，「終於可望迎來短線反彈，但這並未改變我們對後市的整體看法，接下來可能還有下跌空間」。

Krinsky僅找到兩次費城半導體指數出現如此長連跌紀錄的前例，分別發生在2002年與2008年。這兩次指數都曾強勁反彈，隨後卻在接下來幾周再度大幅下挫，跌幅分別達33%與38%。

Kirsch仍認為，現在就宣告修正結束還言之過早。他的分析顯示，標普500指數仍可能下探約7,600點的100日均線。他也與Krinsky一樣，對費城半導體指數抱持疑慮，並將11,000點列為下一個重要支撐。

Kirsch指出，目前部位擁擠程度「已明顯低於夏季」。報告援引Vanda數據指出，科技股曝險已接近中性，近期跌勢應已使曝險進一步降低。

最後，Kirsch指出，科技股走弱是推動美債殖利率下滑的主要力量之一。他對美國10年期公債殖利率的目標為5.00%，之後則看向4.8%。

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow rise, Nasdaq falls to cap volatile week
news.Content: US stock were little changed on Friday as investors tried to look past AI trade-financing worries and turned their focus to upcoming earnings next week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) gained 0.3%, while the Nasdaq 100 ( ^IXIC ) fell 0.5% and the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) remained little changed. All three major averages closed in the green on Thursday. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were on track for weekly losses after a sell-off in chips earlier this week. The Dow, meanwhile, was on pace to finish the week up roughly 1%. Semiconductor stocks edged lower following a volatile week for the sector, a key driver of this year's AI trade. Shares of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave ( CRWV ) came under pressure again on Friday amid concerns over its debt-heavy balance sheet. The stock rebounded on Thursday after Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang voiced optimism about the neocloud provider. Investors have been rotating out of Tech ( XLK ) and into defensive sectors such as Health Care ( XLV ), which climbed to record highs. Tesla ( TSLA ) shares rose more than 1% after the EV maker unveiled a jaw-dropping redesign of the Roadster . Earnings season continues with Tesla on deck for next week. Streaming giant Netflix ( NFLX ) and social media giant Meta ( META ) will also post quarterly results. LIVE 9 updates 1 hr ago Jared Blikre Warsh stays quiet as October hike bets fade and inflation broadens Fed chair Kevin Warsh isn't committing to another rate hike this month, and traders are increasingly betting he'll wait — despite inflation data showing price pressures reaching more of the economy. The odds of an October hike are falling to roughly 15%, according to Bloomberg's bond futures pricing, down from 33% after Wednesday's hot consumer price report and 24% before its release. That retreat began before Warsh spoke at the IMF gathering in Bangkok, where he declined to preview the Fed's next decision . "I don't prejudge meetings," he said. Treasury yields are retreating too. The 10-year yield ( ^TNX ) is hovering near 5.07%, roughly 29 basis points below its October 7 intraday high. The 30-year yield ( ^TYX ) is near 5.42%, down roughly 32 basis points from its peak that same day. Both are edging lower again today. The inflation details are less reassuring. Bank of America calculates that 55% of the core consumer price basket is experiencing three-month annualized increases above 2.5%. Its economists still expect an October hike. That connects to a concern Warsh raised at Jackson Hole in August : how widespread price increases remain. His analysis examined a different inflation measure, personal consumption expenditures, but similarly looked beyond the headline number to gauge underlying pressures. Traders aren't abandoning further tightening. Futures still price roughly one quarter-point hike by December. Watch whether inflation pressures keep broadening when the government releases its PCE inflation report on October 29 following the next Fed decision the day before. Today at 1:45 PM UTC Jared Blikre Visa, Mastercard hit records as chips sink Nearly four in five S&P 500 stocks are advancing this morning, with Visa ( V ) and Mastercard ( MA ) among the companies reaching record highs even as chip stocks extend their selloff. Advancers are outnumbering decliners by nearly 4 to 1, with nearly 400 stocks higher and about 100 lower. Ten of the 11 S&P 500 sectors are gaining, led by financials ( XLF ) and energy ( XLE ). New intraday highs are stretching well beyond the payments sector. MetLife ( MET ), McKesson ( MCK ) and Expeditors International ( EXPD ) are also setting records, alongside ConocoPhillips ( COP ) and Box ( BOX ). The Dow Jones US consumer finance ( ^DJUSSF ) and reinsurance ( ^DJUSIU ) indexes are joining them. Chips remain a different story. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) is losing more than 2%, setting up for a ninth straight decline — the first since 2006. In a Yahoo Finance semiconductor basket, 57 of 60 stocks are falling. Watch whether the broad buying holds through the session. That would strengthen the case that investors are finding alternatives to the struggling AI leaders. Today at 1:34 PM UTC David Hollerith Stocks open Friday mixed US stocks largely held steady at Friday's open as investors looked for direction after a turbulent past few days. At Friday's open, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) gained 0.4% while the the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained 0.1% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell 0.3%. For the week through Thursday, the Dow is up while the Nasdaq is down and the S&P 500 is slightly lower. Today at 1:17 PM UTC Jared Blikre CoreWeave’s bear trap offers fresh bulls hope CoreWeave ( CRWV ) may have trapped fresh bears Thursday. This morning's pullback is testing the bulls. The stock is falling about 5% before the bell after Thursday's dramatic reversal. The stock briefly broke below $60, near its late-July lows, before recovering to finish nearly 6% higher. That's a bear trap — a breakdown that reverses, catching traders betting on further losses. This morning, shares have retraced roughly half the advance from Thursday's low to the overnight high. For technicians, that puts a potential entry for fresh bulls around the midpoint of the rebound — near $65 and change. "First of all, this is more sentiment driven. This is not about fundamentals," BofA Securities senior software analyst Tal Liani told Yahoo Finance when asked what would stop CoreWeave's selling. Liani maintained a Buy rating and $140 price target despite the financing concerns, as my colleague Brian Sozzi reported . The big test remains $60. Holding above it would keep the bear trap intact. A sustained recovery would bring potential resistance around $92–$93 into view, then $120. Losing Thursday's low at $60 would undermine the bullish setup. Today at 1:10 PM UTC David Hollerith Strategy shares fall over 3% as Saylor's bitcoin giant faces index-level threat Stock in Michael Saylor's bitcoin juggernaut Strategy ( MSTR ) fell more than 3% in pre-market trading on Friday after index provider MSCI announced new eligibility rules that could lead to the removal of the bitcoin giant from its global stock indexes. MSCI said Thursday it will adopt new rules to exclude certain "non-operating companies" from its indexes, including those whose primary business resembles that of an investment fund rather than a traditional operating company. Exclusion could include Strategy, the world's largest corporate holder of bitcoin, along with other digital asset treasury companies such as MetaPlanet. Exclusion is expected to force index-tracking funds to sell shares of affected companies. MSCI said it will publish a final list of affected companies on Nov. 11, with the new rules taking effect after the market closes on Nov. 30. Strategy, led by executive chairman Saylor, has previously criticized the proposal as discriminatory against digital asset treasury companies. The company currently holds about 4% of bitcoin's total supply. Today at 12:58 PM UTC Jared Blikre Stocks broadly gaining pre-market as chip selloff continues More S&P 500 stocks are rising than falling before the bell. Chip stocks are still largely heading south. Advancers among S&P 500 constituents are outnumbering decliners by more than 2 to 1, with 224 higher, 106 lower and 173 unchanged. S&P 500 futures ( ES=F ) are edging higher while Nasdaq futures ( NQ=F ) slip. Both remain negative on the week. The stealth stock buying seen this morning extends a broader rotation. Through Thursday, 366 of the S&P's components — 73% — were higher for the week. Since October 6, nearly 70% had advanced, even as the index lost roughly 1%. Chips remain under pressure. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) is falling over 1%, putting a ninth straight loss in play. Its only previous nine-session losing streak ended in May 2006. The fund subsequently fell another 17% through its July closing low two decades ago. Meanwhile, Salesforce ( CRM ) and ServiceNow ( NOW ) are each adding more than 1% after Thursday's rallies. Buyers are lifting 33 of 45 stocks in a Yahoo Finance software basket. Software — ex-cybersecurity — has been a source of strength recently, contrasting with the semis trade. Watch whether that participation survives the opening bell. Continued buying beyond chips would show investors are sticking with alternatives to the struggling leaders. Today at 12:33 PM UTC David Hollerith Regional bank stock Truist falls after 3Q profits miss Shares of Truist Financial ( TFC ) fell more than 2% pre-market after the regional banking giant posted third quarter profits that fell short of analyst expectations. The Charlotte, North Carolina-based lender reported adjusted earnings of $1.16 per share, up 12% from a year earlier but below the $1.19 expected by analysts, according to RBC Capital Markets. Reported earnings were $0.56 per share, reflecting a $1.4 billion loss from selling bonds as part of an effort to reposition its balance sheet. Truist's stock has lagged its rivals since it was born of a so-called merger of equals between BB&T and SunTrust, which closed in December 2019. The bank has since continued to overhaul parts of its business. Truist reported net interest income of $3.66 billion in the third quarter, up slightly from a year ago. The bank also said it moved to further simplify operations in the quarter. Earlier this week, Truist sold $7.7 billion in unsecured consumer loans to private equity giant Carlyle Group. That comes after it sold $5.5 billion in near-prime auto loans to Apollo Global Management last month. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.) "We delivered a solid quarter while also taking decisive actions to better position Truist for the future," the bank's new CEO Mike Lyons said in a statement. Today at 12:30 PM UTC Ines Ferré The US economy is facing two hot wars heating up at a bad time for the White House Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley reports: Yields are above multi-decade highs , both gas and diesel prices continue to climb , and critical midterm elections are around the corner. Adding to pressure on the US economy and the current administration, the world's two largest hot wars are heating up. In the Middle East, dual fronts along the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea have seen a resurgence of conflict in recent weeks that heavily disrupted oil flows in the region. Multiple tankers and container ships in the Strait of Hormuz either caught fire or sank this week in the Iran-dominated waterway. The Washington Institute has tracked more than two dozen attacks recorded since the start of the month. Today at 11:47 AM UTC Ines Ferré Tesla stock pops after unveiling Roadster with compressed air thrusters for limited flight Yahoo Finance's Pras Subramanian reports: After a two-week delay, the Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster event went off with a massive bang — a flying one. The wedge-shaped, cyberpunk-looking Roadster EV appeared in front of an inverted half roller coaster ramp erected at SpaceX's facility in Waco, Texas. The Roadster cruised halfway up — glued to the ramp using a vacuum fan system — then launched off the ramp upside down and performed flips in the air, using air thrusters to right itself and land on the tarmac. Tesla stock rose as much as 5.4% during premarket trading on Friday following the Roadster event. LIVE 9 updates
