news.Title: Here's How Much You'd Have If You Invested $1000 in Monolithic Power a Decade Ago
news.Content:
For most investors, how much a stock's price changes over time is important. This factor can impact your investment portfolio as well as help you compare investment results across sectors and industries.

The fear of missing out, or FOMO, also plays a factor in investing, especially with particular tech giants, as well as popular consumer-facing stocks.

What if you'd invested in Monolithic Power (MPWR) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to MPWR for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?

Monolithic Power's Business In-Depth

With that in mind, let's take a look at Monolithic Power's main business drivers.

Monolithic Power Systems, based in Kirkland, WA, designs, develops and markets high-performance power solutions. The company focuses on the market for high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits (ICs).

Monolithic's products are widely used in industrial applications, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud computing, and automotive and consumer applications.

Being a fabless company, Monolithic works with third-party contractors and chip assemblers for the manufacturing, assembling and testing of wafers and ICs. This approach permits the company to focus more on the designing and development of process technology at a lower fixed cost.

Unlike other fabless semiconductor companies, Monolithic installs its own proprietary process technologies in third-party contractors' equipment and facilities.

Monolithic reported total revenues of $980.6 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Its key product families include, but are not limited to, DC-to-DC, AC-to-DC, driver metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor, power management IC, current-limit switch and lighting-control products.

DC to DC ICs are used to convert and control voltages within a broad range of electronic systems, such as portable electronic devices, wireless LAN access points, computers and monitors, automobiles and medical equipment.

Lighting control ICs are used in backlighting and general illumination products.

By end market, 38.8% of total revenues came from Enterprise Data in the second quarter of 2026.

Storage and Computing, Consumer, Industrial, Automotive and Communications end-markets contributed 20.4%, 5.8%, 5.6%, 16.0% and 13.4%, respectively, to the second quarter of 2026 revenues.

Monolithic's primary competitors are Analog Devices, Infineon Technologies, NXP Semiconductors, ON Semiconductor, Power Integrations, Renesas Electronics, ROHM Semiconductor, Semtech, STMicroelectronics and Texas Instruments.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

While anyone can invest, building a lucrative investment portfolio takes research, patience, and a little bit of risk. If you had invested in Monolithic Power ten years ago, you're probably feeling pretty good about your investment today.

A $1000 investment made in October 2016 would be worth $16,187.64, or a gain of 1,518.76%, as of October 16, 2026, according to our calculations. This return excludes dividends but includes price appreciation.

The S&P 500 rose 263.06% and the price of gold increased 220.64% over the same time frame in comparison.

Analysts are forecasting more upside for MPWR too.

Monolithic is benefiting from expanding power content across AI infrastructure, enterprise data and communications as customers adopt higher-density designs and module solutions. New customer ramps, platform refreshes and DDR5 orders expand its market, while sampling for 800-volt data-center architectures adds a growth avenue. Automotive design wins, robotics activity and building automation extend opportunities beyond core power-management products, while the GlobalFoundries partnership should add capacity and diversify supply from 2027. However, semiconductor cyclicality, high data-center exposure and gross margins near the low end of management's model temper the outlook. Geopolitical uncertainty, execution risk in emerging applications and a premium valuation further limit upside, supporting a balanced view.

Shares have gained 6.81% over the past four weeks and there have been 2 higher earnings estimate revisions for fiscal 2026 compared to none lower. The consensus estimate has moved up as well.

news.Title: Premarket movers: Tesla jumps; Strategy falls on MSCI index threat
news.Content:
Investing.com - U.S. stock futures pointed higher on Friday as concerns surrounding the artificial intelligence boom eased, although the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite remained on track for weekly declines. Investors continued to assess the outlook for AI spending and the potential impact of index changes, while Tesla shares rallied after the company demonstrated its long-awaited Roadster.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

By 05:21 ET, S&P 500 futures had gained 15 points, or 0.2%, while Dow futures climbed 183 points, or 0.4%. Nasdaq 100 futures were mostly unchanged. For the week, the S&P 500 was down almost 1% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite had fallen more than 2%, while the Dow was on course to gain around 1%.

Here are some of the biggest premarket U.S. stock movers today:

Tesla shares rose nearly 5% in premarket trading after the electric vehicle maker unveiled its new Roadster model during a live demonstration on Thursday evening. The event at SpaceX's McGregor, Texas, test facility showcased the vehicle using pressurized air to perform a controlled jump and correct its orientation before landing on all four wheels.

Chief Executive Elon Musk said production of the long-awaited vehicle was set to begin in 2028, adding "actually" as he outlined the timeline. The demonstration renewed investor attention on the Roadster as Tesla continues to develop its broader vehicle and technology ambitions.

Strategy fell 3% in premarket trading after MSCI announced new rules that could result in the company being excluded from its indexes. The decision followed a consultation on the eligibility of non-operating companies and is scheduled to take effect with the November index review.

Under the new methodology, MSCI will assess companies using screens for operating assets and five financial ratios, replacing interim restrictions that had targeted firms with digital asset holdings accounting for at least 50% of total assets. The potential exclusion adds uncertainty for Strategy, whose substantial digital asset exposure has made it a focal point of debates over index eligibility.

Netflix dropped 2% in premarket trading after announcing a leadership change in its content division. Peter Rice, the former chairman of Walt Disney Television, will join the streaming company as chief content officer on October 26, replacing Bela Bajaria, who is leaving after nearly a decade at Netflix.

Story Continues

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

At Disney, Rice oversaw content operations for ABC, FX, Hulu and National Geographic, managing more than 300 shows annually. At Netflix, he will oversee scripted and unscripted series, films and live events across all regions.

CoreWeave fell 3.8% to $67.10 in premarket trading as investors continued to scrutinize the AI cloud computing company's debt burden and the cost of expanding AI infrastructure. Concerns over its approximately $50 billion in debt have weighed on sentiment, amid broader questions about whether future AI revenue will justify the scale of current investment.

The decline came as AI-related stocks faced renewed pressure globally, with investors reassessing the sustainability of spending on data centers and computing capacity.

Cohen & Steers surged 5.8% following its third-quarter 2026 results, which showed $1.6 billion in net inflows. The investment management firm recorded its fifth consecutive quarter of organic growth and its strongest inflow quarter since the fourth quarter of 2021.

Adjusted earnings came in at $0.89 per share, slightly below analyst expectations of $0.92, while revenue increased 11% from a year earlier to $157.4 million. Chief Executive Joseph Harvey said the results provided further evidence that the company's growth strategy was gaining traction, pointing to positive contributions across multiple investment strategies, products and client channels.

Alcoa gained 2.5% after reporting third-quarter results in which stronger-than-expected earnings outweighed a modest revenue shortfall. Adjusted earnings reached $1.82 per share, beating analyst expectations of approximately $1.54, while revenue totaled $3.7 billion, slightly below forecasts but up 24% from the same period a year earlier.

Free cash flow rose to $472 million and adjusted EBITDA reached $789 million, reflecting improved production throughput and operational performance.

Site Centers surged 18.3% after the real estate investment trust announced a $3.00-per-share special dividend and the sale of its stake in the Dividend Trust Portfolio joint venture. The company received net proceeds of approximately $32.4 million from the sale.

The board declared the special cash distribution payable on November 5, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business on October 27. The announcement provided a significant near-term shareholder payout and drove the stock sharply higher in premarket trading.

news.Title: Meet the New Nasdaq-100 Stock That’s Crushing Nvidia, Micron, and Sandisk. Is It Too Late to Buy?
news.Content:
In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) stocks soared in the triple and quadruple digits, leading the S&P 500 higher. Investors rushed to get in on the next big tech growth story, a technology with the potential to transform how many things are done and, as a result, fuel significant gains in corporate earnings. Companies such as AI chip designer Nvidia and memory chip providers Micron Technology and Sandisk have seen their shares skyrocket, and the positive momentum continues today.

But this year, AI stocks haven't been the only growth story. In fact, though they continue to advance, investors have expanded into other industries and turned their attention to new growth opportunities. And this brings me to the stock I'll talk about right here.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

This particular company, a biotech innovator, has seen its shares surge more than 600% this year, largely outperforming Nvidia, Micron, Sandisk, and many other top-performing AI stocks. And just a few days ago, it entered the prestigious Nasdaq-100 , an index that tracks the biggest non-financial Nasdaq companies.

This stock has been a clear winner for investors this year. But after its enormous gain, is it too late to buy now? Let's find out.

Image source: Getty Images.

Moderna's coronavirus blockbuster

The stock I'm talking about has known both tremendous increases and major declines in past years. This company is Moderna (NASDAQ:MRNA), a biotech that made headlines when it brought its coronavirus vaccine from the drawing board to commercialization in less than a year. That was during the early days of the pandemic, and the vaccine, the company's first commercialized product, became a blockbuster, bringing in more than $18 billion at its peak in 2022. Investors piled into Moderna stock, pushing it to a gain of more than 2,000% over about a year and a half.

In recent years, however, Moderna faced significant headwinds. Demand for the vaccine declined in the later days of the pandemic, the company's respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine has struggled to gain market share, and Moderna's much-anticipated cytomegalovirus (CMV) vaccine candidate failed in a phase 3 study.

But Moderna has progressively turned things around. The company cut costs to match the current coronavirus vaccine revenue opportunity , won approval of new products such as a flu vaccine and new coronavirus vaccine updates, and focused its pipeline on oncology and rare diseases in addition to respiratory illnesses. In fact, the progress in oncology has been a catalyst for the stock's performance this year.

Story Continues

Moderna is studying intismeran autogene, a personalized cancer vaccine, in 10 clinical studies, with the most advanced in phase 3. In August, the company announced that intismeran autogene in combination with Merck 's Keytruda met its goals of recurrence-free survival and survival without the spread of disease to distant organs in patients with melanoma. The companies said they would "engage with regulators on filing submissions," suggesting a new product approval for Moderna may be on the horizon.

Surpassing Wall Street's price targets

Moderna had already climbed about 100% this year prior to that news, but the stock soared thereafter, pushing it to gains that surpass those of the AI companies I mentioned earlier. And the stock, trading at around $225, surpasses the average Wall Street 12-month price estimate of $122.

MRNA data by YCharts

Now, let's get back to our question: Is it too late to buy this hot biotech stock? Moderna has a bright future ahead, with new products generating revenue and a late-stage pipeline that should deliver fresh revenue streams moving forward. So Moderna is no longer only a coronavirus vaccine company, and instead is transforming into a larger biotech company with the ability to address a broad range of treatment areas.

Moderna makes a fantastic stock to own, and it should have plenty of room to run in the future as it wins approval for some of its promising pipeline candidates and generates revenue. That said, considering the stock's massive increase this year, I would watch it closely and wait for an opportunity to buy on the dip.

news.Title: Tesla Roadster probably won't drive an earnings beat, but the big reveal did achieve 2 things
news.Content:
The new Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster probably won't be the deciding factor in the company beating on earnings when production possibly begins in 2028, but the high-profile reveal on Thursday night did achieve two things.

"Two takeaways from tonight's Roadster event. 1. It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers. 2. Elon can't wait to bring $TSLA and $SPCX together," veteran tech analyst Gene Munster said in an X post.

It's hard to argue with both points.

Tesla unveiled its redesigned Roadster on Thursday night at SpaceX's ( SPCX ) rocket test site in McGregor, Texas. It came nearly nine years after Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk first showed his idea for the car in 2017.

The wait was worth it.

Using cold-gas thrusters borrowed from SpaceX and a suction system, the car drove upside down on a curved ramp, vaulted off it, and flipped in midair before landing. The car also jumped over a series of Tesla vehicles — not unlike the classic move of K.I.T.T. from the "Knight Rider" TV series.

Musk said it can reach 60 mph in under a second and top 230 mph, though it is unclear whether any of the stunt features would be legal on public roads.

Tesla said production will start in 2028. There is a $50,000 deposit on the Performance version and $250,000 on the Thrust version.

Tesla stock rose 5% in premarket trading on Friday, while SpaceX advanced 2%.

"Wait who the hell was driving the Tesla," Meta ( META ) AI chief Alexandr Wang said on X of the flying Roadster.

Another point well taken.

news.Title: AI概念股估值承壓、資金轉向傳產 法人：美股中期多頭格局未變
news.Content:
美股本周4個交易日呈現高檔震盪且結構大幅分化走勢。受到中東地緣政治緊張推升油價，加上美國公布9月CPI與PPI數據均高於預期，市場對高通膨及美國聯準會潛在強硬立場的疑慮加劇。另一方面，新型雲端服務商Coreweave發行高成本債務引發價值損害疑慮，股債齊跌且信用違約交換（CDS）利差擴大，拖累AI與半導體族群重挫。

道瓊工業指數逆勢上漲1.01%，標普500指數下跌0.85%，那斯達克綜合指數下跌2.39%，費城半導體指數大跌7.88%，羅素2000指數下跌1.41%，NBI生技指數則微漲0.13%。

在經濟數據方面，美國勞動市場表現持穩，初領失業金人數降至19.9萬人；然而通膨壓力明顯回升，9月CPI月增0.6%、年增3.7%，核心CPI月增0.3%、年增2.6%；9月PPI月增1.3%、年增高達6.3%，核心PPI年增5%，均高於市場預期。所幸9月零售銷售月增0.8%，顯示消費韌性仍存。

11大類股呈現漲多跌少，民生消費領漲，科技股則重挫3.94%。半導體與AI產業鏈全面承壓，風暴中心的Coreweave下挫15.1%，美超微電腦下跌16.16%，Dell與慧與科技受評級調降影響重挫約19%至20%，氫燃料電池商Bloom Energy亦重挫15.76%。相較之下，Meta上漲2.51%，蘋果上漲1.59%。金融股整體上漲0.92%，摩根大通因交易業務強勁上漲0.76%，貝萊德管理資產創15.49兆美元新高帶動股價大漲3.55%。

第三季財報季陸續開跑，據彭博與Factset數據，已公布企業中逾6成營收、近8成獲利優於預期。市場預期第三季標普500企業整體獲利將成長29.6%，其中能源、科技與通訊服務獲利力道最為強勁。

富蘭克林股票團隊表示，展望今晚（10/16週五收盤）及下周（10/19-10/23）走勢，美股預計維持「震盪築底、健康輪動」的格局。

市場將高度關注中東情勢及油價波動、川普關稅政策動態，以及密西根大學消費者信心與PMI等數據。同時，下周將有77家標普500企業公布財報（包含特斯拉、Meta、德州儀器等科技巨擘），若財報與展望維持強勁，將為股市提供實質支撐。

團隊認為中期多頭格局未變，雖然高通膨與利率擔憂短期內壓抑科技股估值，但資金並未全面撤出市場，而是從高估值的AI概念股健康輪動至金融、工業、民生消費等實體經濟板塊。

針對當前市場脈絡，富蘭克林股票團隊表示，投資機會正逐漸擴展至更廣泛的族群。AI交易的第一階段獎勵了晶片與基礎設施建造者，下一階段將由將AI付諸實行的公司接棒，如工業、金融、醫療及消費企業，這些企業正藉由專有資料與工作流程重塑經濟結構。此外，算力擴張已從單一晶片轉向整合處理器、記憶體、封裝與軟體的「系統級提升」，推動AI成為通用技術，創新浪潮更將進一步延伸至機器人、基因組學與乾淨能源等領域。

富蘭克林證券投顧指出，地緣政治與油價高檔可能加劇通膨壓力，美聯儲動向與政治不確定性短期內或帶來擾動。然而，在財政刺激、強勁財報與AI資本支出的支撐下，美國經濟基本面依然穩健。近期半導體回檔並未引發全面性崩跌，反而展現健康的類股輪動。長遠來看，美股仍有望維持多頭格局，建議投資人採多元布局，把握工業、金融、消費耐久財及中小型股的輪動機會。

news.Title: Wall St futures mixed as tech wobbles again, Tesla gains
news.Content:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - US stock index futures were mixed on Friday, as technology stocks came under fresh pressure on worries about cracks building in the AI trade, though ‌a rise in Tesla shares and decline in oil prices offered support.

The electric vehicle ‌maker rose 4.4% in premarket trading after unveiling a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX, whose shares ​climbed 2.1%.

Cautionary signs persisted in the AI sector as Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slipped 4.1%, after Thursday's rebound, on lingering concerns about the data centre operator's debt load.

Other neocloud firms Nebius Group and Iren dipped 2% each while chipmakers Micron Technology and Broadcom fell 1.7% and 0.4%, respectively.

AI stocks have cratered this week as investors ‌who have crowded into bets ⁠all along the AI supply chain worry that data centre operators might not turn profitable in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to ⁠rise.

Some of these stocks have risen sharply this year, helping push benchmarks S&P 500 and Nasdaq to record highs as recently as last week.

"When you've this incredibly bullish narrative matched with incredibly bullish outcomes but ​the stock ​declines, that is the sort of technical signal that ​tells you there's too many people ‌in the pool," said James Athey, fixed-income portfolio manager at Marlborough.

The selloff in AI stocks sparked a rotation into defensive sectors such as healthcare on Thursday, helping the main indexes close slightly higher.

Still, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to post weekly losses as an AI-led rout, mixed earnings from big banks and inflation data weighed on sentiment through the week.

The Dow, however, remained on ‌track for a weekly advance.

Markets increasingly expect the Federal ​Reserve to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Fed Chair ​Kevin Warsh said the US economy remained resilient ​and was benefiting from an AI-driven investment boom. He, however, noted the spending ‌surge was boosting inflation.

At 6:21 a.m. ET, ​Dow E-minis were up ​204 points, or 0.39%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 12.5 points, or 0.16%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 23.5 points, or 0.08%.

Further supporting risk appetite, oil prices fell nearly ​1%, though Brent crude remained above ‌the $100-a-barrel mark. [O/R]

Among other movers, Varonis Systems climbed 2.3% after Thoma Bravo's Proofpoint agreed to buy ​the data security firm in a $6.3 billion all-cash deal.

(Reporting by Tharuniyaa Lakshmi in Bengaluru, additional ​reporting by Vidya Ranganathan; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

news.Title: Palantir, Apple and Microsoft Brace for Democrats to Go on Offensive
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- For two years, congressional Democrats furious over corporate America's cooperation with the Trump administration have been limited to the sternly worded letter.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Indonesia Stocks Sink Most in 28 Years on MSCI Downgrade Warning

China's Unloading of US Bonds Gets Fresh Look as Skeptics Grow

Tesla Showcases Long-Awaited Roadster With Aerial Tricks

Stock Buyers Step In to Power Wall Street Rebound: Markets Wrap

CoreWeave's Big Dream Crashes Into Reality as Yields Top 15%

After the midterm elections, some of them will likely have subpoena power. Companies in their sights are armoring up accordingly.

Tech and defense leaders like Palantir Technologies Inc., Apple Inc., and Microsoft Corp. are hiring Democratic Party insiders including former Senator Mark Begich and mega-lobbyist Steve Elmendorf. Other companies that scored contracts helping to facilitate mass immigration raids or sought favor by bankrolling presidential pet projects are scouring internal documents in advance of a push of subpoenas. CEOs are bracing for an uncomfortable inevitability: public testimony before hostile questioners about how they cooperated with a domineering president's demands, and why.

Insiders across K Street describe the flurry of preparations as unprecedented, driven by an acknowledgment of the unusually transactional nature of President Donald Trump's second term — and outrage from Democrats toward those they see as complicit.

While changing political winds always prompt new hires and strategic shifts, prospective Democratic committee chairs are signaling an unsparing blitz that will look to channel voters' anger over alleged corruption and the direction of the economy. With polls indicating Democrats are clear favorites to take back at least one chamber of Congress, corporations are treating the looming confrontation as a crisis — and spending like it's an emergency.

New lobbying registrations have exploded this fall as companies sign up representatives with ties to the Democrats likely to investigate their dealings with Trump, and with experience preparing corporations and CEOs for congressional oversight hearings.

Take some of the companies that donated to the White House ballroom project.

Apple, which hired the Trump-connected lobbyist Jeff Miller during the presidential campaign in 2024, last month tapped Arshi Siddiqui, a onetime aide to former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, to join its roster of lobbyists, advising on "tax, trade and technology-related issues." The company has also hired Liz Allen, a former senior official in President Joe Biden's State Department who served as Tim Walz's chief of staff during his 2024 vice presidential bid.

Story Continues

Microsoft, another ballroom donor, in August reported contracting with Rivendell Group, adding a pair of former Democratic aides to its stable of outside representatives.

And Palantir, which has seen a major expansion in federal contracts over the past two years, has added bipartisan firms to its slate of outside lobbyists. In late spring, the defense contractor hired a team led by Elmendorf, a longtime senior adviser to House Democrats who worked on John Kerry's presidential campaign, and Begich, a former Democratic senator from Alaska.

The Washington Post reported this week on a spreadsheet that tracked $333 million in donations for the ballroom from private donors, including some companies whose contributions hadn't previously been disclosed. Donors included Salesforce Inc., which made a pair of $1 million donations, the Post reported, as well as Marc Benioff, the company's chief executive. Benioff has cultivated a close relationship with Trump as the company has increased its business with the US government.

The software company has also bolstered its lobbying, records show, this summer signing up longtime Democratic lobbyist Mary Beth Stanton, as well as Checkmate Government Relations, a firm with close ties to Trump's inner circle.

Anxiety isn't limited to firms that donated to the ballroom project. One Republican lobbyist said that companies that helped fund Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's "Great American Road Trip" this summer — a group that included many with interests before the department — have expressed concern that they could be called before Congress to explain their interactions with the administration.

Companies that contributed to Trump's inaugural fund, his MAGA Inc. political action committee and various events tied to the country's 250th anniversary, which Trump largely molded into a celebration of himself and his administration, are also worried, this person said.

'Reputational harm'

Potential targets of Democratic scrutiny are generally reluctant to talk publicly, but are bracing for lawmakers to probe anything that smacks of graft.

A prominent financial executive described months of repositioning, including rebalancing political contributions in an attempt to curry favor with the party expected to take power.

A corporate consultant said clients are frantic to avoid being called to explain their cooperation with politically unpopular policies. A K Street lawyer said firms are advising executives to get honest answers ready about their interactions with Trump and his administration's officials — and to comb through internal emails to see what insiders really said about how they were reconciling the president's demands.

The lobbying giant Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck warned in a client alert this month that companies should be preparing now for aggressive oversight, including hearings at which chief executives will be questioned in order to score "political points."

"The practical consequences can be substantial, including reputational harm, stock market impact, executive testimony, extensive document production obligations, parallel regulatory inquiries and legislative initiatives targeting a company's business practices," the memo said.

Democratic strategists say lawmakers can expect heavy pressure from supporters to investigate companies and CEOs with financial ties to Trump and his administration. Lindsay Owens, president of the progressive economic think tank Groundwork Collaborative, says voters across party lines increasingly believe America's political and economic systems are rigged in favor of powerful interests.

"That's now the diagnosis that the American people share — broadly, firmly and coherently," Owens said.

In recent weeks, Owens and her team have been meeting with congressional staff to share a dossier of potential targets for investigation. It includes Tesla Inc. and SpaceX, the behemoths run by Trump ally Elon Musk, as well as Palantir, OpenAI, Amazon.com Inc. and Apple. There's particular interest in companies in the technology industry that benefited from a permissive regulatory posture or tariff carve-outs after contributing sizable donations to the president's inaugural committee or White House projects.

The Groundwork list also names companies outside the tech realm, including McDonald's Corp., Walmart Inc. and Intuit, the parent company of TurboTax. Live Nation Entertainment Inc., which saw an antitrust case with the Justice Department settled after Trump's personal intervention, according to the Wall Street Journal, was also singled out.

'A lot of tension'

Corporate concern has been growing all year, in lockstep with Democrats' increasingly rosy outlook for taking the House, and possibly the Senate, too.

"What may happen if the House does flip is that there will be a lot of hearings, there will be a lot of subpoenas, a lot of tension between the legislative branch and the executive branch over executive privilege and so on," said Peter Orszag, the chief executive of the investment bank Lazard Inc. and the former budget director in the Obama administration, on an earnings call in January.

"It starts with staff asking questions, then a letter, then a request for documents," said Syd Terry, a lobbyist at BGR Group. Terry previously worked for Congresswoman Jan Schakowsky of Illinois when she chaired a consumer protection subcommittee. "By the time anything reaches the hearing room, the story is mostly set. That's what we're telling clients through BGR's oversight working group: The time to prepare is now, not after the first letter arrives."

Veterans of Capitol Hill see plenty of investigative opportunity for Democrats: "There's a lot of red meat there," said the retired Congressman Henry Waxman of California, a crusading liberal Democrat who led investigations and chaired the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform during George W. Bush's administration.

With polls showing rising concern about government corruption, Congress has a duty to investigate, he says. A September Gallup poll found that 89% of US adults say government corruption is "widespread," including large majorities of both Republicans and Democrats.

"It's been eye-opening for the public to see what's been going on under the Trump administration," says Waxman.

Firms that have benefited from the Trump administration's light touch on antitrust enforcement could also be in for particular scrutiny, said Seth Bloom, a lawyer who has represented leading companies and was the longtime general counsel of the Senate's antitrust subcommittee.

Representative Jamie Raskin, a Maryland Democrat, is poised to take over the Judiciary Committee that oversees antitrust issues in the House and recently spoke on the issue at a conference.

"Congressional Republicans have acted like toadies and sycophants, mindlessly rubber-stamping the president's bad deals instead of engaging in meaningful oversight," Raskin said. "They say nothing while shady deals cause prices to go up, wages to go down, and economic disparities to widen."

The recent merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery to create Skydance — and particularly whether the administration's approval hinged on promises about favorable media coverage from impacted networks like CBS News and CNN — could earn particular scrutiny.

"I would expect a lot more oversight," Bloom said. "What happened with these mergers?"

'Hostile administration'

Waxman says Democrats will also "absolutely" want to examine the expansive role Musk has played in the Trump administration as head of the Department of Government Efficiency, calling the tech CEO "an easy oversight target."

But getting answers may be harder than posing the questions. Waxman believes conducting effective oversight will be more difficult than it was during his heyday in the 1990s and 2000s. Congressional staff has been cut in recent years, he notes, leaving committees with fewer investigators to conduct complex inquiries. He also expects the Trump White House to resist investigations.

"It's a hostile administration," says Waxman. "It's much worse today than when I was chairman. I think the executive branch will just shut down any cooperation in giving Congress information. But that only makes the task more vital."

news.Title: As Robotaxis Spread, Carmakers Must Choose Between Owning the Customer and Selling the Car
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA), Alphabet 's (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) Waymo, and Amazon 's (NASDAQ: AMZN) Zoox already operate robotaxis in the U.S., and Chinese operators continue to expand their fleets as the global rollout spreads. Their growth intensifies a critical debate about the future of transportation, which every investor needs to have an opinion on before buying auto-related stocks.

The main players

The future of mobility is autonomy, but it's how that autonomy integrates within transportation that really counts in this debate. On one side are the companies that own the rider via their robotaxis, including Tesla, Amazon, Alphabet, and Uber Technologies (NYSE: UBER), which is building out an autonomous vehicle network in partnership with automakers.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

On the other hand, traditional automakers like Ford Motor Company (NYSE: F) and General Motors (NYSE: GM) abandoned robotaxi development after investing billions. Yet, both continue to work on autonomous driving. They are automakers focused on selling cars, and ultimately, cars with autonomous capability.

There's yet another group in all of this, which includes China's BYD (OTC: BYDDY) and Rivian (NASDAQ: RIVN), which are developing robotaxis but partnering with Uber to allow the latter to build out the network.

The groups can be defined as transportation-as-a-service (TaaS) companies (Tesla, Waymo, and Zoox), automakers with autonomy (Ford and GM), and aggregators (Rivian and BYD), with Uber as a platform owner.

The crux of the debate

The argument centers on the role of electric vehicles (EVs) and their deployment as robotaxis. Although EVs tend to be more expensive up front than traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) cars, they offer a significant cost-per-mile advantage. As such, the optimal use of an EV is as an autonomous robotaxi operating continuously to maximize its cost-benefit.

Consequently, TaaS company leaders, like Tesla Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk, don't believe that robotaxis are an optional extra to an EV business; instead, they see it as the core business. That's why Musk argued on an earnings call in January that "we would make several times more Cybercabs per year than all of our other vehicles combined."

That approach differs from the strategy taken by Ford and GM. GM CEO Mary Barra recently outlined in a CNBC interview that GM wanted to serve the market for personal autonomy, meaning drivers owning the vehicle and using autonomous technology when they want it.

Story Continues

A cynic would argue that Ford and GM might take this approach because they failed to develop robotaxis or develop a foothold in the EV market despite massive investment. Note that Ford CEO Jim Farley told investors in April 2018 that Ford would own and operate a robotaxi network by 2021.

Still, whether it's by design or necessity, selling cars, probably with autonomy in the future, is the approach that Ford and GM are taking. Given the history of personal ownership of transportation, there will likely be a market for them. Whether they develop EVs to capitalize on the shift toward electrification is another question.

Where the robotaxi war will be won

For Tesla bulls, the company's camera-only approach, EV leadership, manufacturing scale, low-cost dedicated robotaxi Cybercab, its enormous accumulation of full self-driving (FSD) data, and its vertically integrated model (which lowers risk of supply chain disruption) create huge structural advantages.

Alphabet (Waymo) and Amazon (Zoox) bulls hope that technological costs will drop, notably for light detection and ranging (lidar), thereby increasing their competitiveness. Meanwhile, Uber is somewhat agnostic about how its autonomous vehicle partners develop hardware/software. In contrast, its partners can bypass the need to handle complex operational matters around robotaxis by being part of Uber's platform.

Those potential partners, including vehicle developers, are using, say, Nvidia 's Alpamayo to develop autonomous driving software.

Which companies will win out?

Tesla and BYD , with some caveats. If Tesla does develop its FSD software as planned and receives regulatory approvals, its structural cost advantages, data, and lack of geofencing will likely create a significant moat, giving it a high lifetime cost and cost-per-mile advantage that Waymo, Zoox, and others will find extremely difficult to compete with. Not least because Tesla already has a more than 50% share of the U.S. EV market. In other words, it's already leading in hardware development.

BYD is also a major player in EVs, and its low-cost vehicles could be a force in the international markets. As for the caveat, if it turns out that Mary Barra is right, the failure to develop new models for the EV market while aggressively ramping up Cybercab production could come back to haunt Tesla down the line. Moreover, Tesla stock is clearly priced with the assumption that its robotaxi rollout will work.

The reality is that the outcome will be somewhere between what Tesla and Barra want: Autonomous robotaxis will induce individuals to forgo personal car ownership, given their lower cost profile, while many consumers continue to favor car ownership. The advantage Tesla and BYD have is that they also hold leading positions in the hardware (EVs) that the market is likely to move toward, whereas the others aren't there yet.

news.Title: 台股大漲他苦嘆「套2年完全沒賺到」 網勸：全砍改買這1檔
news.Content:

news.Content: AI題材帶動台股連續上漲，不少人因此獲利頗豐，不時有人分享獲利可觀的對帳單。但仍有網友好奇，這類文章是否真能反映實際情況，真的人人都賺錢嗎？引發眾人討論。 該名網友在論壇PTT上以「這一年來真的多數都賺錢嗎？」為題發文討論近期的股市投資現象，表示近期經常看到有人在網路上提到這一年多來因AI帶動股市而成功獲利的案例，並貼對帳單佐證投資成果，有些人還開槓桿操作，似乎這陣子每個人都因股市上漲而發大財，但他仍感到懷疑，認為應該還是有人因放空、追高或頻繁交易而虧損。他也好奇，網上一片大賺聲浪的現象，是否是因為獲利的人樂於分享，而賠錢的人多半默不作聲導致的？也想知道投資人的實際情況：「真的是多數人都大賺特賺，賺個100%都算漏氣了？ 非得100萬變成2000萬才算合格？ 都沒有人被洗出去嗎？ 真的多數人都賺錢，而且都100%起跳的嗎？」 ▼原PO表示經常看到網上有人分享投資股市大幅獲利的文章，但他仍有些懷疑，多數投資人的實際情況是否真有這麼樂觀。（示意圖／AI生成） 此貼文吸引許多網友留言討論，有網友表示，台股大盤上漲，的確讓不少人獲利，但並不代表所有投資人都有從中獲利，若尤其是追高個股、放空或使用槓桿的人，仍可能面臨虧損：「倖存者偏差= =賠錢的不會講」、「都賠錢的不好意思說」、「都是聽到個股賠錢，買一些小股本公司」。有些苦主分享自己投資失利的情況：「我空單，有賺有賠，目前-90萬」、「會賠錢的就是槓桿停損仔（我）」。 ▼多數網友認為，今年上半年台股連連上漲，只要不追高個股或過度操作槓桿，穩定投入大盤ETF，大多能獲利。（示意圖／AI生成） 不過，多數網友都認為，上半年逢難得的大多頭市場，加上指數創新高，只要穩定操作，的確讓許多投資人都賺到錢：「正常都賺吧4月追都賺」、「不要追高 不要放空 不要追飆股 都不會賠吧」、「大盤漲了70%，大部分人都賺錢很正常，只是未必賺到70%」、「歷史高點耶，除了空軍之外，要怎麼賠錢？」，還有不少網友提到元大台灣50（0050）及大盤ETF，認為即使是投資新手，只要長期持有這類市值型ETF，在台股頻頻上漲的情況下，想獲利已算相對容易「無腦0050都能賺了，到底怎麼賠」、「買0050會賠嗎？不亂買個股歐印都會賺」、「這兩年買0050放三個月，賺錢的佔9成」、「0050定期定額穩賺，免看盤」、「剩你沒有0050了」，也有人表示「還好我今年主要買大盤，比自己亂買賺的多了」。 （封面示意圖／AI生成）

news.Title: This Dividend King Is Getting In on the AI Energy Boom With Its Recent Deal with Google. Is It a Buy?
news.Content:
Black Hills (NYSE: BKH) is a regulated utility with an impressive 56-year track record of dividend growth . This makes it a Dividend King , or a company that has raised its payout for 50 consecutive years or more.

Regulated utilities have historically been a sleepy part of the stock market because of their low volatility and stable cash flows, but lately they have been making headlines for long-term agreements with major technology companies. On Oct. 6, Black Hills announced multiple agreements with Alphabet 's Google to provide energy infrastructure and services for its hyperscale data center campus in Cheyenne, Wyoming. The agreement runs through 2048 and builds on Black Hills' position as the region's top energy provider for hyperscalers.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Here's what investors need to know.

Breaking down Black Hills' deal with Google

As part of its arrangement with Google, Black Hills will deliver 2.7 gigawatts (GW) of power for Google's data center campus. This includes 590 megawatts (MW) of utility grid-connected service and another 2.1 GW of privately managed, third-party-contracted resources operating as an off-grid microgrid, and boosts Black Hills' position in the region.

Energy services are projected to begin in late 2027 and ramp up to peak operational load by 2030. At that point, Black Hills projects the deal will deliver $150 million in annual net income and $2.4 billion in unlevered free cash flow through 2048.

Under the deal, Black Hills will invest $1.8 billion in capital expenditures to build 564 MW of natural gas power generation between 2027 and 2029. Google provided $399 million in refundable advances for long-lead equipment procurement, which Black Hills plans to reimburse by next year.

Wyoming is emerging as a data center hub

The move helps Black Hills build on its strong regional position. It operates across eight states, including Wyoming, Colorado, Montana, and South Dakota. Cheyenne, Wyoming, has emerged as a data center hub thanks to favorable regulatory policies, a cool climate, and major grid investments.

Wyoming Electric has seen peak electric loads grow over two decades since Black Hills acquired the utility, and its system peak reached a record of 439 MW in July 2026, up 16% from 2025.

Black Hills has partnered with Microsoft in Cheyenne for over a decade and continues to build on that collaboration. In April, Microsoft announced it would acquire 3,200 acres in the area for a new data center capacity under the state's Large Power Contract Service (LPCS) tariff. In addition, Meta Platforms is another hyperscaler building a data center in the region, which is scheduled to open in 2027.

Story Continues

What this means for Black Hills' outlook

The influx of hyperscalers into Wyoming is boosting Black Hills, which is evolving from a sleepy, defensive utility to a key energy infrastructure provider for AI data centers in the region. Its baseline forecast (before its Google deal) includes 600 MW of large data center load through 2030, anchored by Microsoft's and Meta's data centers.

Its deal with Google builds on its strong position, and the $150 million in added net income is massive for the company, which had $292 million in net income in 2025. The company is also a strong dividend stock, with 56 years of raises and a 3.6% yield.

As Wyoming's data center market grows and energy demand surges, Black Hills stands out as an appealing utility stock to capitalize on this growth.

news.Title: Take Five: Earnings, an election and an MSCI headache
news.Content:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - Earnings season is shifting up a gear in the US, and China is about to deliver a deluge of data, giving febrile markets plenty more to ponder after the latest bouts of volatility in bonds and AI stocks.

Central bankers in Indonesia and Turkey have been given headaches by global ‌index provider MSCI, while voters in Brazil gear up to choose their next president.

Here's all you need to know about the coming week in financial markets by Gregor ‌Stuart Hunter in Singapore, Lewis Krauskopf and Rodrigo Campos in New York, Amanda Cooper and Karin Strohecker in London.

1/ EARNINGS SEASON IS HERE

US earnings season picks up in the coming days, with investors focused on Meta Platforms and other ​AI-focused companies as technology shares wobble.

Meta, due on Wednesday, is one of several hyperscalers whose massive spending on AI data centres and infrastructure has been a big driver of investment. With concerns mounting over financing for the AI buildout, investors want more detail on expected returns from those huge outlays.

Reports from semiconductor companies Lam Research and Texas Instruments will offer another view of the AI boom, as will results from Elon Musk's Tesla.

Other high-profile results in the coming days include Netflix, Procter & Gamble and GE Aerospace. S&P 500 earnings are expected to have climbed more than 30% in the third ‌quarter, according to LSEG IBES, continuing a robust year for corporate ⁠profits.

2/ CHINA DATA DELUGE

A health check on the Chinese economy is due on Monday, with third-quarter GDP alongside September retail sales, industrial output and fixed-asset investment data. The latest loan prime rate follows on Tuesday and is expected to stay put after more than a year on hold.

Strong global ⁠demand for semiconductors, clean technology and other manufactured goods has kept China's economy ticking, even as domestic demand remains patchy and higher energy costs bite. Exports have held up despite China's delicate trade balancing act with the US and EU.

The latest trade figures showed Chinese exports surging well beyond analysts' estimates, putting the country on track for another $1 trillion trade surplus this year after crossing the threshold for the ​first ​time in 2025. The flip side: the export boom could add to trade tensions with major partners.

3/ STAIRWAY ​TO HAVEN

For months, as energy and food prices surged amid the Iran ‌war, bonds lost their shock-absorber status as investors jacked up estimates of how high interest rates might need to go.

Story Continues

Add near-chronic concern about developed-world governments' finances, and bonds seemed to offer little safe-haven comfort while still struggling to rival super-charged equities.

The correlation between stocks and bond yields has now turned positive for Europe and the US, meaning yields are more likely to fall when stocks fall. It had been overwhelmingly negative this year, with yields rising as stocks fell, undermining bonds' traditional role as a haven during equity selloffs.

This relationship fluctuates, but this year, the correlation of US stocks and bond yields in March hit its most negative since at least the 1990s, while for European assets, it reached its most negative on record in September.

4/ BRAZILIAN ‌RUNOFF ROULETTE

Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff is keeping markets on edge after Flávio Bolsonaro's surprise first-round lead sent ​stocks up 7.7% and the real almost 4% higher. A new Quaest poll puts Bolsonaro on 46% versus Luiz ​Inácio Lula da Silva's 44%, a technical tie.

Investors are betting a Bolsonaro win would ​bring tighter fiscal policy, but much may already be priced in. His choice of economic team and signs of credible reform could fuel further ‌gains.

A Lula comeback, meanwhile, could put that rally into reverse, with the real, ​longer-dated bonds and state-controlled companies among the most ​exposed. A more conservative Congress, though, could limit how far Lula could shift policy.

5/ AN MSCI HEADACHE

Central bankers in Indonesia and Turkey already have plenty on their plates. Now they have an MSCI headache, too.

Indonesia's central bank meets on Wednesday, while Turkish policymakers gather on Thursday, against a backdrop of high energy prices, rising borrowing costs, AI-driven ​market disruption and geopolitical uncertainty.

MSCI has proposed stripping Indonesia of its ‌emerging-market status and removing it from a suite of indexes, a move that risks triggering heavy outflows and raising pressure on policymakers to hike from 5.75% rather ​than hold.

MSCI has also put Turkey on notice, warning of a potential downgrade if market reforms fall short by mid-2027, another complication for policymakers expected to ​keep cutting rates from 37%.

(Graphics by Prinz Magtulis; Compiled by Karin Strohecker; Editing by Hugh Lawson)

news.Title: 台股本週重挫2202點　上市公司總市值蒸發7.1兆元

news.Title: 台積電跌倒，中小股吃飽！專家曝「3大隱憂」股價拉回即買點
news.Content: 台股今（16）日加權指數收在 47,111.26 點，上漲 141.39 點，成交值為新台幣 9,359.59 億元。護國神山台積電（2330）於法說會後股價出現拉回，收盤下跌 20 元，來到 2,420 元。雖然外資提款導致權王走弱，但盤面卻呈現 「台積跌倒，中小吃飽」 的有趣現象，全台上漲家數達下跌家數的兩倍以上。 財經專家葉育碩 指出，台積電基本面依然強勁，但市場期待過高，並剖析了市場目前擔憂的「3大問題」；不過他也強調，股價適度壓回反而給了投資人撿便宜的機會，若以市場法人預估未來 EPS 達 200 元計算， 長線估值甚至上看 4,000 元。 【台積跌倒中小吃飽！盤面資金出現奇妙輪動】 昨日外資創下台股史上單日鉅額賣超紀錄，導致台積電（2330）短線股價承壓，今日成交量縮至 9,359 億元，顯示不少資金選擇觀望。然而，財經專家葉育碩表示，今天許多中小型股展現強勁反彈，若投資人手中持有的不是台積電而是中小型個股，體感漲跌會截然不同。葉育碩形容，台積電就像每次都考 100 分的優等生，大家都知道它很優秀，偏偏市場期待已被堆高到希望它考 120 分甚至 200 分，因此財報亮眼卻難免面臨高標準的檢視。 葉育碩認為，當台積電股價整理，市場資金可能轉向其他族群，讓中小型股有機會展現行情。不過，資金輪動不代表所有中小型股都會上漲，個股仍須回到營收、獲利、產業趨勢及股價評價等基本面判斷。投資人也不能單憑台積電下跌、大盤上漲，就認定行情已全面轉向中小型股。 【市場熱議！專家曝台積電三大潛在問題】 即便台積電最新財報繳出驚人的營收與獲利，全年美元營收成長展望再度上修，且 2 奈米先進製程與先進封裝動能強勁，但葉育碩特別點出市場網路上對台積電比較擔憂的「三大問題」： 1.巨額資本支出與折舊壓力： 為了擴充 2 奈米及先進封裝，資本支出持續維持高檔，未來廠房設備折舊費用增加，若 AI 需求未達預期，固定成本恐壓縮毛利率。 2.新製程量產初期成本： 2 奈米技術雖遙遙領先，但量產初期設備昂貴且需要時間改善良率，短期對毛利率造成稀釋效果。 3.海外建廠營運成本較高： 美國、日本等地的建廠與營運成本普遍高於台灣，從人力到供應鏈管理，均考驗未來的獲利表現。 【資金轉向中小型股！長線目標價上看4,000元】 葉育碩強調，這些疑慮是市場在高檔時的細節檢視，不代表台積電基本面出了問題。台股不能永遠只有台積電單打獨鬥，當台積電適度休息，資金轉向中小型股，反而能讓整體盤面健全發展。 對於想佈局台積電的投資人，葉育碩認為股價壓回反而是撿便宜的契機。相關券商報告（如元大投顧）預估台積電 2028 年 EPS 可達 197 元，若以整數 200 元計算，給予 20 倍本益比，股價長線估值將高達 4,000 元。在長期成長趨勢不變的前提下，目前的拉回整理，正好提供投資人冷靜思考與分批建立部位的空間。

news.Title: 台股站回4萬7! 小彈141點 周K翻黑跌2202點
news.Content:
[ 非凡新聞 ]記者黃友柔,攝影張皓普

受到國際股市回穩激勵，台股今（16）日跌深反彈，盤中一度上漲超過500點，重新站上4萬7。不過，台積電股價未止跌，收盤收在最低2420元，雖然還有權值二哥聯發科帶領大盤上攻，不過指數終場漲勢收斂，僅上漲141點，收在47111點，周線終止連四紅，成交量大約9360億元。籌碼方面，三大法人賣超678億元，雖然比起前一天收斂，但累計本周合計賣超7093億，其中，外資提款5900億元。

股民：「股市將近5萬點了，我覺得風險意識還是要有，不是說那麼好賺，不然大家都不用上班了。」

股民：「很多人樓高起、樓高垮，我自己是有先在48600到5萬點之間一直減碼。」

經過前一天的震撼教育，股民們操作小心翼翼，就算台股16日反彈，但是護國神山台積電法說會後股價幾乎都在平盤下游走。

群益投顧董事長 蔡明彥：「短期間基本上還是中東的危機再次的波動，可能會導致一些資金上的波動，所以行情基本上會比較震盪一點，另外一個波動或許也跟美國選舉大家擔心的，因為目前共和黨的一個聲勢基本上是比較落後的，大家都擔心說民主黨上台之後，是不是對AI的投資來講的話會踩煞車，或者說環評的部份在再趨嚴，會導致很多計畫的一個延宕，那這個部分來講可能也是近期有些資金開始做一些提前反應的原因。」

觀察指數在本周最後一個交易日，又成功站回4萬7，市場資金流向PCB、光電等族群，台郡再奔漲停、台虹等軟板概念股跟著上攻；另外傳產股同樣吸金，台塑化攻上漲停價，而大型權值股中聯發科、鴻海也紛紛回神。

不過籌碼面外資持續提款，一周下來總共賣超台股近5900億元，儘管投信砸888億元護盤，三大法人單周合計仍賣超7093億元。

統一投顧董事長 黎方國：「目前普遍的看法，明年指數的高點應該都會上看5萬5千點，我想離現在都還有很大的距離，我想對明年的看法也相對是比較樂觀的，第三個就是第四季有集團作帳的行情，那加上就是旺季行情，我想經過了這個短暫剛才講的三個變數之後，我想這個股市應該還會再重拾一個多頭的格局，期中選舉之後是一個很好的布局的點，美股基本上都是上揚的。」

法人對明年行情依舊樂觀，投資人現在除了期待看到指數再創新高，更期盼手中獲利跟著報到。（記者黃友柔、張皓普／台北採訪報導）

news.Title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has Over 45% of Berkshire Hathaway's $356 Billion Portfolio Invested in 3 Undeniable Winners
news.Content: This has been a game-changing year for Berkshire Hathaway 's (NYSE:BRKA)(NYSE:BRKB) long-term shareholders. Warren Buffett's retirement on Dec. 31 meant that this trillion-dollar conglomerate entered the year without its most familiar face running the show for the first time in well over half a century. However, the Oracle of Omaha's successor, Greg Abel, hasn't missed a beat. He's grabbed the bull by the horns and revamped several aspects of Berkshire's $356 billion investment portfolio , while keeping one key trait the same: concentration. Abel, like Warren Buffett , has more than 45% of Berkshire Hathaway's invested assets ($160.6 billion) in just three undeniable winners: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), American Express (NYSE:AXP), and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)(NASDAQ:GOOG). Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Portfolio concentration has always been important to Warren Buffett and his successor, Greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images. Apple: $76.73 billion (21.6% of invested assets) Apple was Warren Buffett's No. 1 holding by market value for close to a decade leading up to his retirement. Although innovation has always been the driving force behind Apple's success, Buffett tended to appreciate the company's exceptional pricing power and consumers' affinity for the brand. But the Oracle of Omaha dumped 75% of Berkshire's stake in Apple in the nine quarters leading up to his departure. This left the door open for Abel to potentially continue selling shares after he took over as CEO. However, Abel's first annual letter to shareholders in February referred to Apple as one of a few concentrated holdings that's expected to "compound over decades." Though this doesn't rule out further sales of Apple stock, it's pretty evident that Berkshire's new boss appreciates what Apple brings to the table: leading domestic smartphone sales (iPhone) and the world's largest share repurchase program. American Express: $46.72 billion (13.1% of invested assets) Greg Abel is also overseeing a true legacy holding in American Express (commonly known as "Amex"). Amex has been a continuous holding for Berkshire Hathaway since 1991. Financial stocks were always a favorite for Buffett because they're cyclical. Berkshire's now-former boss understood that while recessions are inevitable, they're historically short-lived. Buying bank stocks and financial services providers enabled Berkshire to take advantage of long-winded economic expansions. Story Continues American Express thrives as a double-dipper. It collects fees from merchants when processing transactions, as well as annual fees and interest income from cardholders as a lender. Furthermore, Berkshire is netting a nearly 45% annual yield on cost from its Amex stake, giving Abel virtually no reason to ever sell this position. Image source: Getty Images. Alphabet: $37.17 billion (10.5% of invested assets, both share classes combined) However, Warren Buffett's successor really made his mark by piling into Google parent Alphabet. Abel more than tripled Berkshire's stake in the first quarter and added another $17 billion during the June-ended quarter. There's little doubt that Abel, like Buffett, appreciates Alphabet's virtual monopoly in internet search. According to GlobalStats, Google accounted for roughly 90% of global internet search traffic in September, highlighting its impressive ad-pricing power. But it's Alphabet's artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions that have piqued Greg Abel's interest. Since Alphabet integrated generative AI and large language model capabilities into Google Cloud, the world's No. 3 cloud infrastructure services platform by total spend, sales have skyrocketed. We may be witnessing the birth of an AI applications powerhouse in Google Cloud. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity. While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook. Continue » American Express is an advertising partner of Motley Fool Money. Sean Williams has positions in Alphabet. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Alphabet, American Express, Apple, and Berkshire Hathaway. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy . news.Title: 《陸股》滬指漲0.24%、週K連四黑；創業板指跌0.39%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-16 17:26:39 數位內容中心 發佈

中國A股今(16)日震盪分化，上證指數收於3,716.28點，上漲8.80點或0.24%，惟日K連三黑；深證成指收於11,802.46點，下跌14.33點或0.12%；創業板指收於2,772.38點，下跌10.79點或0.39%；科創50收於1,358.65點，下跌0.87點或0.06%。盤勢呈現早盤走高、尾盤回吐的走勢，指數表現明顯分歧。

依盤勢來看，上證指數相對抗跌並收紅，但深證成指、創業板指與科創50走弱，顯示成長族群承壓較重。盤中雖一度走強，但午後多次回檔，市場資金在追價與獲利了結之間快速切換。

以週線來看，上證指數本週跌2.56%、週K連四黑；深證成指跌6.64%、週K連四黑；創業板指跌8.90%、週K連四黑。成交量方面，滬市今成交7,325億元(人民幣,下同)，深市成交8,229億元，兩市成交額1兆5,554億元，較前一交易日量縮約5%。

從盤面上來看，軍工成為盤面主線，航發科技、長城軍工、晨曦航空等表現強勢。低空經濟概念同步活躍，萬豐奧威、中信海直等走揚。此外，房地產類股也有明顯表現，深物業A、新城控股等走高。福建本地股同樣走強，福建水泥、廈門信達等同步上漲。

科技與創新藥方面，記憶體、半導體午後回暖，瀾起科技、兆易創新等出現修復；但PCB、銅箔基板與部分創新藥、CRO族群回檔。盤面顯示，科技類股內部分歧仍大，資金尚未形成一致主線。

news.Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella Just Shared Bad News for Nvidia and Great News for This Rival Chipmaker
news.Content:
Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) is planning a big change to its Azure cloud computing data centers starting next year. It will rely much more on its custom-designed silicon than on leading graphics processing units (GPUs) like those from Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). It's already made significant progress in expanding workloads for its Maia 200 chips, and it expects its next-generation Maia 300 chips to deliver significant improvements when it starts deploying them next year.

"Starting next calendar year, we will scale our Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments, making it the primary inference system for our own product and services," CEO Satya Nadella said. That's great news for its custom chip partner, Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL), and bad news for Nvidia.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia is losing data center market share

Nvidia's extreme dominance of the data center GPU space during the first few years of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom left its market share with nowhere to go but down. Its biggest customers, including the hyperscalers and leading AI frontier labs, have developed custom solutions that can handle AI workloads, and that can deliver better price performance on specific tasks than Nvidia's GPUs.

That said, GPUs offer far greater flexibility in terms of the types of tasks they can perform, making them particularly valuable for companies deploying servers to sell compute capacity to third parties with dynamic demands. Notice that Microsoft is starting its Maia expansion by focusing on its own products and services, not on leasing Maia compute capacity to third parties looking to cut costs on their OpenAI GPT-based applications.

Their use, though, could expand over the long run. Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), which has been building its own custom AI chips for longer than any of its competitors, has seen strong adoption of its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) by its Google Cloud customers for training and inference. Apple used TPUs to train Apple Intelligence, and Anthropic is using gigawatts worth of TPUs to develop its large language models.

While Nvidia can continue to grow sales extremely quickly, other chipmakers' growth rates are likely to outpace it. That's reflected in its P/E valuation, which now sits below those of its biggest rivals.

Story Continues

Microsoft could be Marvell's fastest-growing customer

During its 2026 investor day this month, Marvell said it expects that it will grow its share of the custom AI accelerator market over the next five years. Its work on the Maia 300 is likely a big reason why. Microsoft's plan to make that processor the primary inference system for its products and services is in line with earlier reports that it will make a big step up in custom silicon orders starting next year.

The revenue opportunity for Marvell is huge. Microsoft will spend approximately $175 billion in capital expenditures on data centers over the next year. Roughly two-thirds of that will go toward servers and networking equipment. If Marvell takes just a sliver of that spending, it would amount to a huge boost to its revenue, which totaled just $9.5 billion over the last four quarters.

Marvell believes the combination of its custom AI chips and its networking chips will help it grow revenue tenfold over the next five years. That is to say, Microsoft's ramp-up in Maia chips is just the start. Marvell also signed a deal with Google earlier this year to design and sell inference-optimized versions of its TPU chips. The deal also gives Alphabet the option to take a stake in Marvell.

Considering Marvell's growth potential, the stock's forward P/E of 63 looks inexpensive. If you look out to its fiscal 2029 (which mostly takes place in calendar 2028), the stock trades at just 21 times earnings estimates. Given its potential to capture a significant slice of the market for data center AI processors, that seems like a good price to pay.

news.Title: UK competition regulator targets Microsoft's business software grip
news.Content:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - Britain's competition watchdog proposed on Friday to designate Microsoft with "strategic market status" in business software, a move that could pave ‌the way for interventions in how the US tech major bundles ‌products such as Excel, Teams and its Copilot AI assistant.

The Competition and Markets Authority launched in ​May an investigation into whether Microsoft's bundling of its business software products, which have around 20 million monthly users across the UK, was uncompetitive.

The regulator found that the company has a strong position across key areas of digital activity, including personal ‌computer operating systems and ⁠productivity software suites, and that its strength in business software comes from the barriers customers face when switching.

A Microsoft spokesperson said ⁠it did not share the CMA's views in its proposed decision.

"All our products — including Copilot — are open and interoperable, giving customers the ability to use them alongside competing ​services," ​the spokesperson said.

The CMA is also further ​assessing whether customers can freely choose ‌AI tools and whether rivals can compete with Copilot, whether the company's bundling of security products limits choice, and the impact of its licensing practices on customers' cloud deployment options.

The regulator will invite views on the proposed designation and will then make a final decision by February.

If the proposal goes through, it ‌would make Microsoft the third company subject to ​Britain's new digital market powers. Google received strategic ​market status in online search ​and in mobile platforms, and Apple received strategic market status ‌in mobile platforms, all in October ​2025.

In June this year, ​the CMA imposed new conduct requirements on Google's search services, including allowing publishers to stop their content being used to power the US tech ​major's AI features.

It also ‌ordered Google to provide greater transparency on how its search rankings ​work.

(Reporting by Yadarisa Shabong in Bengaluru and Paul Sandle in London; ​Editing by Jochelle Mendonca and Janane Venkatraman)

news.Title: Not AMD. Not Broadcom. This is the Chip Designer Nvidia Investors Should Be Watching
news.Content:
Many Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) investors warily monitor Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO). And for good reason. AMD competes directly with Nvidia. Broadcom co-develops custom silicon for companies such as Alphabet 's (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) Google to help them reduce their dependence on Nvidia.

However, there's another chip designer that Nvidia investors should be watching closely. This company isn't even really a rival to Nvidia. But without it, Nvidia is unlikely to be successful going forward.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

A lucrative Nvidia connection

I won't try to build the suspense: The chipmaker I'm referring to is Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM). In some ways, Arm ranks as the most important semiconductor stock other than Nvidia itself.

Arm's business model makes it unique from AMD, Broadcom, and other chipmakers. The company licenses its architecture, then collects royalties on every chip manufactured using its designs. Some have described the ongoing intense competition between semiconductor makers as the "chip wars." By that analogy, Arm is the top weapons supplier to many major combatants.

Nvidia is a key customer for ARM. The Vera CPUs built to run agentic artificial intelligence (AI) are built on Arm's architecture. When Nvidia recently projected a stunning $20 billion in Vera CPU sales by the end of the current fiscal year, it was understandably great news for Arm.

Arm has already made a huge inroad into the data center CPU market, though. Its customers include the big three cloud providers -- Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), and Google. Arm executive vice president Mohamed Awad recently told Nikkei Asia in an interview that his company has captured "over 50%" of the hyperscaler market, adding, "The tailwinds are running with us."

An impressive growth trajectory

Throughout most of this year, Arm's stock outperformed nearly every other semiconductor stock. It's still handily beating Nvidia and Broadcom, although a recent pullback now has Arm trailing behind AMD.

This stock performance is backed up by strong financial growth. Arm's revenue jumped 22% year over year in the first quarter of its fiscal year 2027 to a record high of roughly $1.3 billion.

Royalty revenue comprised around 55% of that total, reaching $715 million. This bodes well for Arm going forward. When royalties from chips sold that use its architecture generate more revenue than upfront licensing deals, the company's revenue stream is more predictable.

Story Continues

Don't think Arm's licensing momentum is waning, though. Licensing and other revenue increased 23% year over year in fiscal Q1 to $574 million. Management said this growth was "driven by continued strong demand for Arm IP [intellectual property]."

Is Arm stock a buy?

Regardless of which company wins the smartphone and AI chip races, Arm benefits. All the top competitors in these markets use Arm's architecture -- and pay royalties for the privilege. Not even Nvidia, the largest technology company on the planet based on market cap, can make that claim.

Does this make Arm stock a no-brainer buy? Not quite. There's one nagging little detail about Arm that investors can't ignore: its steep valuation.

Arm's shares currently trade at more than 150 times forward earnings. Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom look dirt cheap by comparison. For that matter, so does every other large-cap stock that operates in the semiconductor industry.

Normally, that kind of nosebleed-level valuation would send analysts headed for the hills. Wall Street remains bullish about Arm, though. Of the 22 analysts who have rated the stock over the past three months, 17 recommended buying it. The consensus 12-month price target reflects a potential upside of roughly 19%.

This enthusiasm among analysts underscores the critical role that Arm plays in the chip market. Arguably, no company is more aligned with Nvidia's growth than Arm. Investors must pay a lofty premium to own this stock, but sometimes that premium is worth it.

news.Title: Warsh avoids rate guidance; Tesla’s Roadster turns in air - what’s moving markets
news.Content:
Investing.com - Futures linked to the major U.S. averages point higher, after equities on Wall Street advanced in the prior session, rebounding from an artificial intelligence-driven selloff earlier in the week. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh declines to provide specific interest-rate guidance ahead of the central bank's October policy meeting, but says he has spoken with global central bankers about mounting inflationary pressures. Some investors reportedly temper their valuations for Claude-maker Anthropic's potentially massive initial public offering, while Taiwan is said to be mulling over stricter export controls on AI chip sales to China. Elsewhere, Tesla's latest sports car turns in the air.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

1. Futures higher

U.S. stock futures hovered above the flatline on Friday. By 02:59 ET (06:59 GMT), the Dow futures contract had risen by 75 points, or 0.1%, S&P 500 futures had ticked up by 7 points, or 0.1%, and Nasdaq 100 futures were broadly unchanged.

The main averages all finished higher on Thursday, bouncing back from a downturn fueled by jitters around a growing debt pile financing the AI boom and worries over elevated borrowing costs. In particular, shares of neocloud CoreWeave, whose precipitous slide on Wednesday helped spark the global rout in AI stocks, stabilized.

"Financial markets have calmed a little after CoreWeave stock bounced on Thursday. But the debate between intensifying price pressures needing tighter monetary policy and a tech correction requiring a softer policy outlook continues," analysts at ING said in a note.

2. Fed's Warsh avoids signaling October rate decision

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh offered an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy, saying he was surprised how resilient it has proven to be in the face of tighter monetary policy.

But speaking at an event in Thailand, Warsh also said he had spoken with other central bankers about inflationary pressures. He added that it is "hard to be in a discussion" with these central bankers and "not compare notes and hear the same thing about the surge in prices."

As he has largely done since taking over at the helm of the Fed earlier this year, Warsh did not reveal any specific insight into the central bank's rate trajectory. Instead, he stressed that he doesn't "believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year."

Story Continues

Despite Warsh's resistance to forward guidance, some of his Fed colleagues have suggested in recent weeks that while further rate hikes may be needed to corral inflation, they are awaiting more data. In September, the Fed lifted borrowing costs by 25 basis points, highlighting a desire to cool price growth back to its 2% level.

Markets are widely betting that the Fed will stand pat on rates at its October 27-28 gathering. Earlier this week, wagers on a potential hike this month briefly increased following hotter-than-anticipated consumer price data, but later dissipated. Instead, rates are tipped to move up by a quarter of a percentage point again at the Fed's final meeting of the year in December.

3. Investors temper Anthropic IPO valuations - Reuters

Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its possible blockbuster initial public offering are mulling over a lower valuation for company after a financial disclosure this week, according to Reuters.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The high-profile AI frontier lab has reportedly been eyeing a major IPO as soon as November, bringing to public markets a firm whose Claude chatbot has made it one of the figureheads of the AI era.

Some investors who attended meetings with Anthropic in San Francisco on Wednesday discussed a valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion, which would be down from a previously projected valuation of around $2 trillion.

Media reports said Anthropic told investors at the gathering that its third-quarter revenue had jumped by 45% to $16.8 billion. While the figure indicated robust demand for Anthropic's cutting-edge AI tools, analysts flagged that the revenue growth rate slowed sequentially.

4. Taiwan eyeing stricter controls on AI chip sales to China - Bloomberg

Taiwan is considering much stricter export controls on artificial intelligence chip sales to China as part of a greater alignment with the U.S., Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The considerations -- which are part of an effort to address chip smuggling risks -- are aimed at giving authorities more legal tools to address diversion of advanced hardware, chiefly AI servers with Nvidia chips, from Taiwan to China, the Bloomberg report said.

Such a measure risks drawing more ire from Beijing, which has already balked at strict U.S. restrictions on AI chip exports to China -- first imposed in 2022.

But Nvidia's advanced AI chips were still seen making their way into China, through reported smuggling through Southeast Asia.

5. Tesla unveils new Roadster with rocket-style thrusters

Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster on Thursday evening which used SpaceX rocket technology to jump off a ramp and perform a controlled landing.

CEO Elon Musk said production of the long-awaited vehicle was set to begin in 2028, over a decade after it displayed a next-generation version of its electric sports car.

Shares of Tesla rose over 3% in extended hours trade following the reveal.

The company debuted the model in a live event at SpaceX's McGregor, Texas test facility. The vehicle was able to climb a curved ramp at a controlled pace and jump the ramp at a full inversion before using its air thrusters to correct its orientation and land on all four wheels. Tesla also had the car jump and fly over a set of parked cars and a semitruck.

(Reuters contributed reporting)

news.Title: 外資賣股匯出壓不住！新台幣週五盤中貶破32.5元，收盤仍貶7.3分
news.Content:
【財訊快報／劉敏夫】台北外匯市場週五新台幣兌美元匯價走貶、尾盤貶勢明顯收斂，台幣在本週先後兩次爆出巨量重挫後延續近日貶勢。儘管週四美元走弱給予台幣一些喘息空間，但台積電財報未能明顯激勵風險情緒，仍見外資持續匯出。週五台股上揚，加權指數收漲0.30%，但是外資賣超上市股票461.4億元，連八日淨賣超。新台幣兌美元匯率週五以32.338元作收，與前一交易日比較，台幣匯率貶值7.3分。銀行間新台幣兌美元最高成交價落於盤初為32.250元，最低成交價為午間的32.520元，成交量為32億9,300萬美元。

以未獲授權公開評論為由要求匿名的兩位外匯交易員表示，公股銀行雖較上日更為積極賣出美元，但仍不敵外資大量匯出的資金，使得台幣上午貶破32.5元價位。出口商於美元/台幣32.5元之上才有意願賣出美元，但是金額不大。同時，外資部分匯出的資金仍在消化週四賣超台股的金額。

台積電週四繳出優於預期的第三季財報及展望，但還是未能消除市場對於AI建設熱潮可持續性的擔憂，而且儘管週四相關擔憂開始吸引避險資金低接美債而壓抑美元，美、台利差仍不利於台幣。

華僑銀行經濟專家Herbert Wong表示，全球拋售AI資產的壓力，使得外資匯出的情況未見顯著的改善，對台幣持續造成壓力。情況要見好轉需要外資轉向匯入，而台灣央行的干預可減少波動度。32.525為目前關鍵點位。

news.Title: Sandisk Stock Could Be Worth $4,128 in the Next Year
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) stock has already delivered an extraordinary run this year, up about 497% year-to-date, as of Oct. 13, 2026. There are risks with storage stocks, given the past boom-and-bust cycles in product pricing. However, the stock, currently priced at $1,416, has a realistic shot at nearly tripling to $4,128 over the next year or so, provided demand for storage and memory continues to outstrip supply and remains strong.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

CEO says Sandisk is still in the early innings of AI-driven growth

On the August 2026 earnings call, CEO David Goeckeler called AI inference a memory-centric, storage-intensive problem reshaping demand for NAND flash memory. Its leadership in this market is translating into broader customer adoption.

Revenue grew 51% quarter over quarter to $9 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter. Management expects revenue to grow approximately 17% sequentially in fiscal first-quarter 2027, to between $10.3 billion and $10.8 billion. Adjusted ( non-GAAP ) earnings per share (EPS) are expected to be between $44 and $46.

Sandisk is selling more high-speed solid-state drives (SSDs) to big cloud and AI companies that need fast storage for their most demanding computing tasks. In the latest quarter, it also began shipping a new, higher-capacity product called Stargate, designed for the massive data collections that AI systems create and use.

Over the last year, data center storage has grown from roughly 12% of the company's total bits shipped to 38%, making it Sandisk's fastest-growing market.

Goeckeler said he believes Sandisk is still in the early innings of this opportunity. That outlook aligns with broader AI spending trends. Goldman Sachs Research forecasts that global AI-related investment will exceed $1 trillion this year.

Sandisk's path to a $4,300 share price

The risk for any storage stock is cyclical price fluctuations. However, new long-term agreements with eight customers are expected to cover more than half of bits shipped in fiscal 2027 and two-thirds in fiscal 2028, providing greater visibility into revenue and earnings.

At the current $1,416 share price on Oct. 14, 2026, the stock is trading at a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 19.2. Applying the same trailing multiple to the $215 consensus fiscal 2027 earnings estimate puts the share price at $4,128 next year.

Story Continues

Still, it's difficult to predict how the market will value the stock. If the market senses greater risk of a downturn in storage and memory pricing, or a stall in the AI spending boom, it may value the shares at a lower P/E multiple. Therefore, the stock may not deliver nearly as much upside.

Based on Goeckeler's comment on the runway of growth still ahead, I think the stock is worth buying. Top memory supplier Micron Technology is mostly sold out of advanced memory for 2027, and at higher prices than in 2026. This points to broad market demand for storage and memory that will continue to benefit Sandisk. Even a modest P/E on next year's earnings would send Sandisk stock price over $2,000 in 2027.

news.Title: 為胡正明新書站台 魏哲家笑說來「放鬆」：台積電股價跌心情不好
news.Content:
昨日台股遭遇重挫，今天台積電董事長魏哲家現身力挺「三維電晶體之父」胡正明舉行的新書發表會，魏哲家一開口就開玩笑說，「準備法說會很累，原本就想過法說會後股價會跌，結果真的跌了，所以心情不太好」，因此來新書發表會放鬆一下。

對書名《拿出辦法來》好有感觸 竟是創辦人張忠謀常說

前一天才開完法說會，隔天台積電董事長魏哲家出席台積電首任技術長、三維電晶體之父胡正明的新書發表會。上台時魏哲家坦言「現在腦袋有點空，為了準備法說會，緊張了一陣子」。而昨日台股遭遇重挫，魏哲家就笑說，「本來就知道股票會降，果然降了，所以心情非常不好，好在來這邊稍微紓解一下」。

魏哲家也對書名《拿出辦法來》好有感觸，表示看到這本書名字心裡嚇一大跳、壓力排山倒海而來，因自己也拿到一模一樣的牌子。原來這句是台積電創辦人張忠謀常對團隊說的話，後來他將這句話刻在水晶牌上，送給幾位高階主管，而胡正明也拿到了，這也成了這群精英們共同記憶，讓魏哲家感嘆，「當你的老闆告訴你拿出辦法來的時候，表示你沒有辦法」。

書名《拿出辦法來》，正是台積電創辦人張忠謀常對團隊說的話。圖／台視新聞

胡正明新書發表會重量級嘉賓雲集 魏哲家寫推薦序

新書發表會現場重量級嘉賓雲集，包括世界先進董事長方略、旺宏電子總經理盧志遠、美國國家科學院海外院士朱敬一等人。胡正明也分享請魏哲家寫推薦序的小故事，說是自己突然生病，有一天魏哲家就出現，就趁機問他可不可以寫一個序。

news.Title: 美股漲勢凌厲 永豐金證券複委託衝破2846億元
news.Content:
伴隨今（2026）年前三季S＆P 500上漲12.7％，漲幅落在歷史上第四季85％機率續漲的區間，永豐金證券以複委託金額2,846億元，寫8月市場之冠，市佔率逾2成，月成長22％近乎超車所有同業。永豐金證券表示，要以旗下下載破百萬次的數位投資APP「大戶投」三大精準「選、投、速」美股功能，助攻用戶搶得布局先機。

利率升、就業弱但成長熱，今年美股在「攀越憂慮之牆」（Climbing the Wall of Worry）中持續走升，進入過去25年來平均表現相對亮眼的第四季。1950至2025年的歷史經驗顯示，當S＆P 500當年度前三季累計漲幅介於10％至20％時，第四季延續漲勢的機率高達85％。今年前三季漲幅正落在該區間，使市場對第四季行情更添期待。

加上11月下半月向來是美股歷史勝率最強勢時段之一，2001至2025年之間，S＆P 500與Nasdaq-100上漲機率皆達80％，美股年底旺季行情是否上演，格外備受關注。永豐金證券分析，目前AI投資熱潮正在沿著半導體、記憶體及光通訊等供應鏈上游搬家，加上算力基礎建設黃金時代才剛開始，產業輪動與個股分化已經是美股投資新顯學，這讓今年美股用戶投資個股比重達86％，其中未滿20歲亦高達78％。

為幫助投資人精準捕捉「哪些個股最具成長潛力」，永豐金證券大戶投APP推出三大精準選美股功能，看盤、下單一個APP完成。第一，導入獨家分析師評級、股息與殖利率，簡單輕鬆掌握心中優質股；第二，提供Nasdaq企業級即時報價，與華爾街行情光速對焦，零時差抓買點，目前全體用戶已完成免費升等；第三，提供「便宜成長股」、「便宜價值股」等策略選股條件。

news.Title: PCB與記憶體強攻，台股急彈後開高走低！外資賣壓改善前留意追高風險
news.Content:
【財訊快報／黃冠豪】亞洲股市昨日重挫過後，今日迎來跌深反彈。美股道瓊前一晚大漲556點，帶動市場避險情緒降溫，日本日經225指數今強勁反攻，終場上漲898.34點，漲幅1.39%，半導體設備、AI科技股成為反彈主力。台股昨日狂瀉1,655.96點，今日早盤隨亞洲股市同步反彈，加權指數一度大漲550.73點，最高來到47,520.60點，不過，台積電(2330)等尾盤賣壓出籠，指數漲幅大幅收斂，終場上漲141.39點，漲幅僅0.30%，收在47,111.26點，成交金額9,378.93億元。櫃買指數上漲3.36點，漲幅0.85%，收在400.26點，中小型電子股表現優於大型權值股。惟集中市場外資連八賣，今日再倒貨461.47億元，外匯市場同步出現大量貶值。大型權值股今日呈現分歧，台積電法說會釋出樂觀展望，但股價不漲反跌，終場下跌20元，收2,420元，跌幅0.82%；聯發科(2454)上漲85元，收4,250元，漲幅2.04%；台達電(2308)上漲5元，收1,635元；聯電(2303)收133元，下跌0.5元，跌幅0.37%。熱門族群方面，PCB、ABF載板及記憶體成為今日反彈焦點。PCB受到輝達OCP高頻材料題材帶動，台郡(6269)、台虹(8039)、華通(2313)盤中攻上漲停，富喬(1815)、金像電(2368)同步吸引買盤。ABF載板包括欣興(3037)、南電(8046)、景碩(3189)出現跌深反彈，顯示資金重新回流AI高速傳輸供應鏈。

記憶體族群表現亮眼，南亞科(2408)、華邦電(2344)、旺宏(2337)盤中同步走強，晶豪科(3006)一度大漲逾9%兵臨漲停，反映市場對記憶體景氣的期待。被動元件則呈現個股分化，鈺邦(6449)、勤凱(4760)相對強勢，國巨(2327)、華新科(2492)則面臨高檔震盪。

面板級封裝方面，友達(2409)、群創(3481)的玻璃基板與FOPLP題材持續受到關注，友達更擠進成交量排行榜前段。矽光子、光通訊族群則相對疲弱，聯亞(3081)、華星光(4979)、聯鈞(3450)盤中承壓，顯示AI族群資金仍以選股為主。

今日最大焦點仍是台積電法說會效應，Q3單季EPS達29.43元，全年美元營收成長預估上修至44%，2027年2奈米產能預計增加超過一倍，並評估赴美國德州設廠，以及與馬斯克Terafab計畫合作的可能性。另外，經濟部長龔明鑫透露，台灣計畫在美國設立多座AI供應鏈產業園區，首座預計落腳德州，投資規模最高40億美元，協助台灣AI供應商赴美布局。美光台中先進封裝測試二廠昨日正式啟用，也為台灣HBM與AI記憶體供應鏈帶來新的發展契機。

台股今日雖然成功收復47,000點，但早盤大漲逾500點後漲幅明顯收斂，顯示上檔解套與外資獲利賣壓仍重。下週應觀察台積電能否止跌，以及PCB、記憶體、被動元件與矽光子族群能否延續資金輪動。短線47,000點為重要觀察關卡，48,000點則是反彈壓力區。在外資賣壓尚未明顯改善前，仍應留意追高風險。

GPU基建公司COREWEAV週四在資金成本上升陰影中黑翻紅、收漲近6%，加上美國10年債殖利率拉回，帶動美股四大指數多收紅，不過費城半導體指數連續第七天下跌、收跌0.88%。亞洲股市方面，因日經225指數昨日暴跌3,318點，創下史上第3大單日跌點，吸引投資人逢低買進，終場上漲1.39%；韓國股市同步反彈，KOSPI指數終場上漲2.05%。
